entry.title: SAP Document and Reporting Compliance: e-Invoice in Contract Accounting (FI-CA) using Extensibility
entry.content:
You want to enable your system to create electronic documents for invoices posted via Contract Accounting (FI-CA) using SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. In this blog, we'll show you an example of how this can be achieved using extensibility, with the Netherlands (NL) as a reference country.

Before you begin, ensure that the Financial Accounting Document, Sales and Distribution Billing Document e-Invoicing option is already available in your system for the specific country, including the eDocument customization and eDocument process. An implementation overview note (ex: for NL 2424637 ) will be available for each country e-Invoicing process if the country is localized by SAP for Financial Accounting Document, Sales and Distribution Billing Document. If you need to set up e-Invoicing from scratch for your country without an existing FI/SD localization, refer to Extensibility for Electronic Document Processing in Private Cloud.

Implement the following SAP Notes before proceeding:

3337374, 3342537, 3331737, 3332372, 3381485, 3387690, 3406988, 3413057, 3406213 — these notes enable e-invoice for Contract Accounting and trigger eDocument creation from all relevant transaction codes.

Important: Download and activate the BC Sets attached to notes 3331737 and 3381485.

Steps to Create Electronic Documents

1. Configure the eDocument Type Table

Customize the eDocument: Accounting Document Type for FI-CA view (V_TFK003EDOC2) for your country to determine the eDocument type based on the type of FI-CA document.

Example configuration for Country/Region NL:

ApAreaDoc. TypeDescriptionOriginDoc. Origin DescriptioneDocument TypeType DescriptionDoc. No. Source
Extended FI-CA04Reversal02ReversalNL_CRENetherlands Credit NoteOPBEL – FI-CA Document Number
Extended FI-CA05Dunning Notice11Dunning Run DocumentNL_INVNetherlands eInvoiceOPBEL – FI-CA Document Number
Extended FI-CAABGeneral Document01Manual PostingNL_INVNetherlands eInvoiceXBLNR – External Reference Number
Extended FI-CAAEManual Inv with Edoc01Manual PostingNL_INVNetherlands eInvoiceOPBEL – FI-CA Document Number
Extended FI-CAAFEU Manual Inv w Edoc01Manual PostingEU_INVEU eInvoiceOPBEL – FI-CA Document Number
Extended FI-CACEEU creditnote w Edoc01Manual PostingEU_CREEU Credit NoteOPBEL – FI-CA Document Number
Extended FI-CACNCreditNote withEdoc01Manual PostingNL_CRENetherlands Credit NoteOPBEL – FI-CA Document Number

Replace NL_INV and NL_CRE with the eDocument types defined for your country (e.g. XX_INV, XX_CRE).

2. Create the eDocument Class

Create a new class ZCL_EDOCUMENT_XX_CA (replace XX with your country code) and set the superclass to CL_EDOCUMENT_EU_CA if you use the PEPPOL network, or CL_EDOCUMENT_XX for others. 

Example for NL — class CL_EDOCUMENT_NL_CA with superclass CL_EDOCUMENT_EU_CA.

Add a CONSTRUCTOR method with the following parameters:

ParameterOptionalTyping MethodAssociated TypeDefault Value
IO_SOURCE_DATA✓Type Ref ToCL_EDOC_SOURCE 
IV_EDOC_GUID✓TypeEDOC_GUID 
IV_LAND✓TypeLAND 
IV_UPDATE_TASK✓TypeSAP_BOOLABAP_FALSE
IV_GENERIC_BADI_FILTER_ADAPTOR✓TypeEDOC_GENERIC_BADI_FILTER 
IV_SIMULATE_FOR_EMAIL_OPTION✓TypeABAP_BOOLABAP_FALSE

Exception: CX_EDOCUMENT — eDocument exceptions

Example constructor logic (for Country NL):

METHOD constructor.

    CONSTANTS lc_edocument_class TYPE edoc_class_name VALUE 'CL_EDOCUMENT_NL_CA'.

    TRY.
*       Call Constructor of the superclass
        super->constructor( io_source_data                 = io_source_data
                            iv_edoc_guid                   = iv_edoc_guid
                            iv_land                        = iv_land
                            iv_update_task                 = iv_update_task
                            iv_generic_badi_filter_adaptor = COND edoc_generic_badi_filter(
                                                               WHEN iv_generic_badi_filter_adaptor IS NOT INITIAL
                                                               THEN iv_generic_badi_filter_adaptor
                                                               ELSE cl_edoc_source_fica_document=>gc_src_fica_document ) ).
      CLEANUP INTO DATA(lx_edocument).
    ENDTRY.

    "Determine handling class (own class name)
    ms_edocument-edocument_class = lc_edocument_class.

    "Define source document type as generic BAdI filter to separate BAdI implementations

    "Filter for adaptor already put to super->constructor
*   ms_generic_badi_filter-adaptor     = lv_generic_badi_filter_adaptor.

    "Filter for intf.conn. no more needed, standard impl. contains CI enhancement spot
*   ms_generic_badi_filter-interf_conn = cl_edoc_source_fica_document=>gc_src_fica_document.

    ms_generic_badi_filter-partner_conn = cl_edoc_source_fica_document=>gc_src_fica_document.

ENDMETHOD.

Redefine the following methods:

DETERMINE_PROCESS — assigns the correct process and process version based on the eDocument type and interface type. Replace NL with your country of choice.

METHOD determine_process.

    CASE ms_edocument-edoc_type.
      WHEN 'NL_INVIN'.
        ms_edocument-process         = 'NLINVIN'.
        ms_edocument-process_version = '0001'.
      WHEN OTHERS.
        CASE ms_edocument-interface_type.
          WHEN 'AIF_PROXY' OR 'STANDARD'.
            ms_edocument-process         = 'NLINV'.
*           reference process is 'EUINV'
            ms_edocument-process_version = '0001'.
          WHEN OTHERS.
            MESSAGE e162(edocument) INTO gv_error_txt.
            raise_edoc_exception( ).
        ENDCASE.
    ENDCASE.

ENDMETHOD.

ADD_PARTICIPANT_DOCTYPE — adds participant and document type information specific to your country.

Parameter

Type
IV_DOC_TYPETYPE STRING
IV_DOC_CATEGORYTYPE STRING
CT_PARTICIPANT_DOCTYPETYPE MTT_PARTICIPANT_DOCTYPE
METHOD add_participant_doctype.

    TRY.
        DATA(lo_edoc_nl) = NEW lcl_edoc_nl_friend( ).

        lo_edoc_nl->mo_source    = mo_source.
        lo_edoc_nl->mo_adaptor   = mo_adaptor.
        lo_edoc_nl->mo_process   = mo_process.
        lo_edoc_nl->mo_interface = mo_interface.
        lo_edoc_nl->ms_edocument = ms_edocument.

        lo_edoc_nl->add_participant_doctype(
          EXPORTING
            iv_doc_type            = iv_doc_type
            iv_doc_category        = iv_doc_category
          CHANGING
            ct_participant_doctype = ct_participant_doctype
        ).

        ms_edocument = lo_edoc_nl->ms_edocument.

      CATCH cx_edocument.
    ENDTRY.

ENDMETHOD.

GET_PROC_STEP_VARIANT — determines the process step variant for routing.

ParameterType Spec.Description
EV_PROC_STEP_VARIANTTYPE EDOC_PROC_STEP_VARIANTeDocument Process Step Variant
EV_IS_PROCSTEPVAR_DETERMINEDTYPE ABAP_BOOL 
EV_IS_PROCSTEPVAR_OVERWRITTENTYPE ABAP_BOOL 
METHOD get_proc_step_variant.

    TRY.
        DATA(lo_edoc_nl) = NEW lcl_edoc_nl_friend( ).

        lo_edoc_nl->mo_source    = mo_source.
        lo_edoc_nl->mo_adaptor   = mo_adaptor.
        lo_edoc_nl->mo_process   = mo_process.
        lo_edoc_nl->mo_interface = mo_interface.
        lo_edoc_nl->ms_edocument = ms_edocument.

        lo_edoc_nl->get_proc_step_variant(
          IMPORTING
            ev_proc_step_variant          = ev_proc_step_variant  " eDocument Process Step Variant
            ev_is_procstepvar_determined  = ev_is_procstepvar_determined
            ev_is_procstepvar_overwritten = ev_is_procstepvar_overwritten
        ).

        ms_edocument                  = lo_edoc_nl->ms_edocument.
        mv_is_procstepvar_determined  = abap_true.
        mv_proc_step_variant          = ev_proc_step_variant.
        mv_is_procstepvar_determined  = ev_is_procstepvar_determined.
        mv_is_procstepvar_overwritten = ev_is_procstepvar_overwritten.

      CATCH cx_edocument.
    ENDTRY.

ENDMETHOD.

PROCESS_REQUEST_SEND — handles the sending of the eDocument request.

ParameterType Spec.Description
IV_INTERFACE_GUIDTYPE EDOC_INTERFACE_GUID OPTIONALInterface Message ID
IV_PROCESS_STEPTYPE EDOC_PROCESS_STEP OPTIONALeDocument Process Step
IV_VARIANTTYPE EDOC_PROC_STEP_VARIANT OPTIONALeDocument Process Step Variant
value(RV_RESULT)TYPE EDOC_PROC_STEP_RESULTeDocument Process Step Result
CX_EDOCUMENT eDocument exceptions
METHOD process_request_send.

    DATA: lv_variant                    TYPE edoc_proc_step_variant,
          lv_is_procstepvar_overwritten TYPE abap_bool.

    TRY.
        get_proc_step_variant(
          IMPORTING ev_proc_step_variant         = lv_variant
                    ev_is_procstepvar_overwritten = lv_is_procstepvar_overwritten ).

        IF lv_is_procstepvar_overwritten IS INITIAL.
          lv_variant = iv_variant.
        ENDIF.

        super->process_request_send(
          EXPORTING
            iv_interface_guid = iv_interface_guid
            iv_process_step   = iv_process_step
            iv_variant        = lv_variant
          RECEIVING
            rv_result         = rv_result ).

      CATCH cx_edocument.
    ENDTRY.

ENDMETHOD.

With these settings you should be able to create an eDocument and view it in transaction EDOC_COCKPIT.

3. Create the AIF Mapping Class

Create a mapping class ZCL_EDOC_MAP_UBL_CA_XX for your country.

  • For PEPPOL countries: set the superclass to CL_EDOC_MAP_UBL_CA.
  • For non-PEPPOL countries: set the superclass to CL_EDOC_MAP_XX

Example for NL — class CL_EDOC_MAP_UBL_CA_NL with superclass CL_EDOC_MAP_UBL_CA.

Redefine only the methods necessary for your country where the super class does not cover country-specific functionality.

Example for NL: The methods FILL_CUSTOMER_PARTY and FILL_SUPPLIER_PARTY are redefined to handle Netherlands-specific party data requirements.

FILL_CUSTOMER_PARTY

Parameter: value(RS_CUST_PARTY) TYPE EDO_UBL_ACCOUNTING_CUSTOMER_PA — Proxy Structure (generated)

METHOD fill_customer_party.

    CALL METHOD super->fill_customer_party
      RECEIVING
        rs_cust_party = rs_cust_party.

    CLEAR: rs_cust_party-party-endpoint_id-base-base-content,
           rs_cust_party-party-endpoint_id-base-base-scheme_id.

    TRY.

        DATA(lo_ubl_nl) = NEW lcl_ubl_nl_friend( iv_ns           = CONV #( mv_ns )
                                                  io_edoc_map_ubl = me        ).

        IF mv_customization_id CS mc_customization_id_bis3.
          lo_ubl_nl->fill_endpoint( EXPORTING iv_partner   = mv_gpart
                                    IMPORTING ev_endpoint  = rs_cust_party-party-endpoint_id-base-base-content
                                              ev_scheme_id = rs_cust_party-party-endpoint_id-base-base-scheme_id ).
        ENDIF.

        lo_ubl_nl->read_kvk_or_oin( EXPORTING iv_partner        = mv_gpart
                                    IMPORTING ev_party_id        = DATA(lv_party_id)
                                              ev_party_id_type   = DATA(lv_party_id_type)
                                              ev_party_code_type = DATA(lv_party_code_type) ).

        "Get BPTAXNUM to use with fill_party_tax_scheme
        read_vat_number_for_partner( EXPORTING iv_partner = mv_gpart
                                     IMPORTING ev_taxnum  = DATA(lv_bptaxnum) ).

        CLEAR rs_cust_party-party-party_tax_scheme.
        rs_cust_party-party-party_tax_scheme = lo_ubl_nl->fill_party_tax_scheme(
                                                 EXPORTING iv_bptaxnum = CONV #( lv_bptaxnum )
                                                           iv_land     = ms_source-source_header-land
                                                           iv_partner  = mv_gpart ).

        DATA(lv_partner_name) = ms_adrc_bupa-name1.

        rs_cust_party-party-party_legal_entity = lo_ubl_nl->fill_party_legal_entity(
                                                   EXPORTING iv_registration_name = CONV #( lv_partner_name )
                                                             iv_party_id           = lv_party_id
                                                             iv_party_id_type      = lv_party_id_type
                                                             iv_party_code_type    = lv_party_code_type ).

      CATCH cx_edocument.
    ENDTRY.

ENDMETHOD.

FILL_SUPPLIER_PARTY

Parameter: value(RS_SUPP_PARTY) TYPE EDO_UBL_ACCOUNTING_SUPPLIER_PA — Proxy Structure (generated)

METHOD fill_supplier_party.

*   CALL METHOD SUPER->FILL_SUPPLIER_PARTY
*     RECEIVING
*       RS_SUPP_PARTY =
*       .
    rs_supp_party = NEW lcl_ubl_nl_friend( iv_ns           = CONV #( mv_ns )
                                            io_edoc_map_ubl = me
                                           )->fill_supplier_party( ).

ENDMETHOD.

4. Maintain the Required Customizations

Configure the following views using transaction SM30:

View EDOFACTORYV — Classes for generating eDocument instances:

Source TypeFactory Class
FICA_DOCCL_EDOC_FACTORY_FICA_DOC

View EDOMAPCLASSDETV — Assign a mapping class to each process and Interface ID:

eDocument ProcessProcess VersionInterface IDeDocument TypeSource TypeMapping ClassDirection Description
EUINV1UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_RESPONSEXX_CREFICA_DOCCL_EDOC_MAP_UBLInboundUBL Credit Note Response
EUINV1UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_TRANSMXX_CREFICA_DOCCL_EDOC_MAP_UBL_CA_XXOutboundUBL Credit Note Transmission
EUINV1UBL_INVOICE_RESPONSEXX_INVFICA_DOCCL_EDOC_MAP_UBLInboundUBL Invoice Response
EUINV1UBL_INVOICE_TRANSMXX_INVFICA_DOCCL_EDOC_MAP_UBL_CA_XXOutboundUBL Invoice Transmission

View EDOPROCSPINTDETV — Process Step Interface Determination. Add 4 entries as shown below:

eDoc. processVersProcess StepeDoc. TypeSource TypeInterface ID
EUINV1REQ_SENDXX_CREFICA_DOCUBL_CREDIT_NOTE_TRANSM
EUINV1REQ_SENDXX_INVFICA_DOCUBL_INVOICE_TRANSM
EUINV1SENDEDOCXX_CREFICA_DOCUBL_CREDIT_NOTE_TRANSM
EUINV1SENDEDOCXX_INVFICA_DOCUBL_INVOICE_TRANSM

View EDOPROCSTEPDETV — Process Step Determination. Add 4 entries as shown below:

eDoc. ProcessVersInterface IDeDoc. TypeSource TypeProcess StepDirection
EUINV1UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_RESPONSEXX_CREFICA_DOCPROC_RESPInbound
EUINV1UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_TRANSMXX_CREFICA_DOCSENDEDOCOutbound
EUINV1UBL_INVOICE_RESPONSEXX_INVFICA_DOCPROC_RESPInbound

Communication with Tax Authorities

If Financial Accounting Document, Sales and Distribution Billing Document e-Invoicing option is already available in your system for the specific country, you will be able to submit your Contract Accounting eDocument which is created above without any additional set up. If you need to set up the communication, you can refer to the above guide Extensibility for Electronic Document Processing in Private Cloud.

entry.title: Introduce yourself to the group.
entry.content:
Olá a todos!

O meu nome é Manuel e sou um dos membros da Comunidade SAP. Hoje gostaria de iniciar uma iniciativa online divertida. Vou responder a algumas perguntas para me apresentar e, em seguida, marcar outras pessoas. Depois, quando for a vossa vez, poderão marcar outras pessoas, permitindo-nos embarcar numa jornada incrível para nos conhecermos melhor.

Portanto, vou começar:

Quem sou eu e de onde sou? Sou Arquiteto e Consultor Sênior SAP especialista em Finanças e Controlling (FI/CO), além de Gerente de Projetos PMP® e membro ativo do PMI (capítulo Fortaleza). Ao longo da minha carreira internacional, tenho-me dedicado a transformar a complexidade de negócios em soluções tecnológicas eficientes, unindo uma sólida bagagem técnica, visão estratégica e forte liderança comunitária. Tenho raízes firmes em Portugal e uma forte conexão com o Brasil — o país onde vivo em Fortaleza desde 2010 com a minha esposa Kelzia e onde construí a minha família. Carrego também a sensibilidade artística de quem na juventude foi clarinetista na Banda Filarmónica de Crestuma. Porque, no fim das contas, a trajetória tem-me ensinado que um passo de cada vez e o compromisso inegociável com a excelência são o que nos levam ao objetivo.

O meu tópico SAP e o que me apaixona mais? Sou profundamente apaixonado por Finanças SAP, Controlling, auditoria de dados e arquiteturas de integração de APIs financeiras (tais como APIs bancárias e suítes de pagamento), transformando processos financeiros complexos em realidades otimizadas e automatizadas.

Como foi a minha jornada no mundo SAP? A minha história com a tecnologia começou muito cedo: aos 14 anos, trabalhei como serralheiro na construção de autocarros na UTIC, em Vila Nova de Gaia, estudando à noite para concluir o curso técnico de Eletrotecnia. Essa dedicação levou-me à Universidade Portucalense, no Porto, onde me formei em Matemática Aplicada e Informática, concluí posteriormente o meu Mestrado em Desenvolvimento de Software e onde também tive o privilégio de atuar como docente, lecionando a cadeira de ERP SAP no curso de Sistemas de Informação para Gestão. Como consultor SAP focado nas áreas Financeira e Controlling, busco constantemente a excelência multidisciplinar, complementando a minha formação com uma Pós-graduação em Controladoria e Finanças e outra em Desenvolvimento de Software. Sou também um ávido produtor de conhecimento: escrevo assiduamente artigos técnicos compartilhando as minhas vivências profissionais (disponíveis em mrobalinho.blogspot.com.br) e atuo ativamente como palestrante e participante assíduo de eventos da comunidade SAP.

Como foi a minha experiência no SIT e qual a sessão que mais me marcou? Estando profundamente envolvido como um dos principais organizadores do SAP Inside Track Fortaleza (que já vai na sua sétima edição) e colaborando com o SAP Inside Track Porto, cada evento é uma fonte incrível de inspiração. Mais do que qualquer sessão técnica específica, o que verdadeiramente me marcou em toda esta jornada foi a gratidão demonstrada pelas associações a quem destinamos o saldo remanescente dos eventos e toda a arrecadação de bilheteira. São normalmente instituições que trabalham com crianças, idosos e pessoas desfavorecidas, onde cada moeda faz toda a diferença. Vê-los presentes nos eventos a apresentar as suas turmas de música e canto faz com que todo o nosso esforço e dedicação valham a pena, reforçando o nosso papel como genuínos dinamizadores e apoiantes da comunidade que nos rodeia.

A minha jornada na Comunidade SAP: Organizar comunidades como o SAP Inside Track Fortaleza e o SIT Porto tem sido uma das partes mais gratificantes da minha carreira, promovendo colaboração, mentoria e crescimento além-fronteiras.

Com quem seria feliz por me conectar? Como me interesso muito por Arquitetura Financeira, SAP BTP e Construção de Comunidades, adoraria conhecer pessoas que partilham destas mesmas paixões.

Gostaria de passar o testemunho a: @ [Pedro Vieira], @ [Matheus Brazil], @ [João Vieira] e estou ansioso por ver as vossas respostas às perguntas partilhadas acima!

 

======  EN Version =======

Hello everyone!

My name is Manuel and I am a member of the SAP Community. Today I would like to start a fun online initiative. I will answer a few questions to introduce myself and then tag other people. Then, when it's your turn, you can tag other people, allowing us to embark on an incredible journey to get to know each other better.

 

So, let's begin:

 

 

Who am I and where am I from? I am a Senior SAP Architect and Consultant specializing in Finance and Controlling (FI/CO), as well as a PMP® Project Manager and an active member of the PMI (Fortaleza chapter). Throughout my international career, I have dedicated myself to transforming business complexity into efficient technological solutions, combining solid technical background, strategic vision, and strong community leadership. I have firm roots in Portugal and a strong connection with Brazil — the country where I have lived in Fortaleza since 2010 with my wife Kelzia and where I built my family. I also carry the artistic sensibility of someone who, in his youth, was a clarinetist in the Crestuma Philharmonic Band. Because, in the end, the journey has taught me that one step at a time and an unwavering commitment to excellence are what lead us to our goal.

My SAP topic and what I'm most passionate about? I am deeply passionate about SAP Finance, Controlling, data auditing, and financial API integration architectures (such as banking APIs and payment suites), transforming complex financial processes into optimized and automated realities.

What was my journey in the SAP world like? My story with technology began very early: at 14, I worked as a locksmith in bus construction at UTIC, in Vila Nova de Gaia, studying at night to complete my technical course in Electrotechnics. This dedication led me to the Portucalense University in Porto, where I graduated in Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, later completing my Master's degree in Software Development, and where I also had the privilege of working as a lecturer, teaching the SAP ERP course in the Information Systems for Management program. As an SAP consultant focused on Finance and Controlling, I constantly seek multidisciplinary excellence, complementing my training with a postgraduate degree in Controlling and Finance and another in Software Development. I am also an avid producer of knowledge: I regularly write technical articles sharing my professional experiences (available at mrobalinho.blogspot.com.br) and actively participate as a speaker and regular attendee at SAP community events.

 

What was my experience at SIT like, and which session stood out the most? Being deeply involved as one of the main organizers of SAP Inside Track Fortaleza (which is already in its seventh edition) and collaborating with SAP Inside Track Porto, each event is an incredible source of inspiration. More than any specific technical session, what really stood out to me throughout this journey was the gratitude shown by the associations to whom we donate the remaining balance from the events and all the ticket revenue. These are usually institutions that work with children, the elderly, and disadvantaged people, where every coin makes all the difference. Seeing them present at events presenting their music and singing lessons makes all our effort and dedication worthwhile, reinforcing our role as genuine facilitators and supporters of the community around us.

My journey in the SAP Community: Organizing communities like SAP Inside Track Fortaleza and SIT Porto has been one of the most rewarding parts of my career, promoting collaboration, mentorship, and growth beyond borders.

Who would I be happy to connect with? As I am very interested in Financial Architecture, SAP BTP, and Community Building, I would love to meet people who share these same passions.

I would like to pass the baton to:  @[Pedro Vieira], @[Matheus Brazil], @[João Vieira] and I look forward to seeing their answers to the questions shared above!

entry.title: Re: We're Improving Result Limit Settings to SAC Tables - Tell Us What Admins Need
entry.content:
Hi @JefB,

one example are client calculations or also custom cells. You can reference cell in these calculations, which are not available in the first loaded resultset when using lazy loading. These calculations would then show wrong results or an error state.

Issues can also arise when you try to rank or sort a client calculation. That is only possible if the whole result set is available as these calculations are done in the frontend and not pushed down. 

That being said, we are now actively investigating how we can unblock lazy loading in story tables at least for the majority of use cases. 

Best

Anna

entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Here is the response our internal chatbot provided. Please check whether it helps you resolve the error.

Kind regards,

Henrike

#AI-Generated Content

MDG BP Governance — Custom UIBB Not Refreshing After 2025 Upgrade

Root Cause Analysis

The silent failure (no errors, but UIBB empty) after an upgrade almost always falls into one of these categories. They should be investigated in this order:

Cause 1 — UIBB Reads from Persistence, Not the Delta Buffer (Most Common)

Before the 2025 upgrade, the FPM page lifecycle may have triggered a full round-trip that accidentally caused the UIBB to re-read. Post-upgrade, the lifecycle is tighter and the UIBB must explicitly read from the delta buffer.
In your custom UIBB's GET_DATA / DO_INIT / PROCESS_EVENT:
METHOD get_uibb_data.
 
DATA: lo_delta_read TYPE REF TO if_usmd_delta_buffer_read,
lt_zleg_po TYPE TABLE OF your_zleg_po_structure,
lv_found TYPE abap_bool.
 
" *** ALWAYS read from the DELTA BUFFER, not SELECT from DB ***
lo_delta_read = mo_gov_api->get_buffer( )->get_read_access( ).
 
lo_delta_read->read_data(
EXPORTING
iv_entity_type_name = 'ZLEG_PO' " Your custom entity type
is_selection = VALUE #(
( fieldname = 'KEY_FIELD'
option = 'EQ'
sign = 'I'
low = ms_key-key_field ) )
IMPORTING
et_data = lt_zleg_po
ev_data_found = lv_found
).
 
IF lv_found = abap_false.
" Buffer entry does not exist yet — handle gracefully
RETURN.
ENDIF.
 
" Bind to your UIBB context node
mo_context_node->set_attribute(
EXPORTING
iv_attr_name = 'TABLE'
iv_value = lt_zleg_po ).
 
ENDMETHOD.

Cause 2 — Cross-Entity BAdI Writes with Wrong Change Mode

In MDG 2025, write_data without an explicit iv_change_mode defaults differently than in prior releases. You must pass the correct mode, especially for insert/update on Type 4 custom entities.
Corrected cross-entity BAdI derivation:
METHOD if_usmd_rule_service~derive.
 
DATA: lo_buffer_write TYPE REF TO if_usmd_delta_buffer_write,
ls_zleg_po TYPE your_zleg_po_structure,
lt_zleg_po TYPE TABLE OF your_zleg_po_structure.
 
" --- Derive your custom entity from the standard PO/SO ---
" (your existing derivation logic here)
MOVE-CORRESPONDING is_purchase_org TO ls_zleg_po.
ls_zleg_po-custom_field_1 = ... " legacy mapping
APPEND ls_zleg_po TO lt_zleg_po.
 
" --- Write to delta buffer ---
lo_buffer_write = io_services->get_buffer( )->get_write_access( ).
 
lo_buffer_write->write_data(
EXPORTING
iv_entity_type_name = 'ZLEG_PO'
" *** CRITICAL: explicit change mode required in 2025 ***
iv_change_mode = if_usmd_delta_buffer_write=>co_change_mode_insert_update
it_data = lt_zleg_po
).
 
" --- IMPORTANT: Invalidate any cached read for this entity ---
" This forces the UIBB to re-fetch on next render
io_services->get_buffer( )->invalidate_read_cache(
iv_entity_type_name = 'ZLEG_PO' ).
 
ENDMETHOD.
Note: The constant name for change mode varies slightly by MDG release — check your system for co_change_mode_insert_update vs gc_change_mode_update in IF_USMD_DELTA_BUFFER_WRITE.

Cause 3 — UIBB Not Flagged for Refresh After BAdI Execution

In FPM / MDG 2025, the NEEDS_REFRESH method is evaluated more strictly. Your UIBB must signal it needs to re-render whenever the underlying buffer changes.
In your UIBB class, override NEEDS_REFRESH:
METHOD if_fpm_ui_building_block~needs_refresh.
 
" Option A: Always refresh (safe but slightly less performant)
rv_needs_refresh = abap_true.
 
" --- OR ---
 
" Option B: Check if the custom entity buffer was touched (preferred)
DATA: lo_delta_read TYPE REF TO if_usmd_delta_buffer_read.
lo_delta_read = mo_gov_api->get_buffer( )->get_read_access( ).
 
lo_delta_read->has_pending_changes(
EXPORTING
iv_entity_type_name = 'ZLEG_PO'
IMPORTING
ev_has_changes = rv_needs_refresh
).
 
ENDMETHOD.

Cause 4 — FPM Event Not Raised to Trigger UIBB Re-render

If the BAdI derivation runs on a button press or value-help select, you must explicitly raise an FPM event to cause UIBBs to re-render. This used to happen implicitly in older MDG versions.
Raise FPM event after the derivation (e.g., in the BP Governance Controller):
DATA: lo_fpm TYPE REF TO if_fpm,
lo_event TYPE REF TO cl_fpm_event.
 
lo_fpm = cl_fpm_factory=>get_instance( ).
 
" Raise standard MDG refresh event
lo_event = cl_fpm_event=>create_by_id(
iv_event_id = if_usmd_gov_api=>gc_event_data_changed ).
 
lo_fpm->raise_event( io_event = lo_event ).

Cause 5 — Custom Type 4 Entity Not Registered with the UI Refresh Framework (2025-Specific)

In MDG 2025, there is an internal registry that tracks which entity types participate in the reactive UI refresh. Standard entities are pre-registered; custom Type 4 entities must be registered via customizing or the BAdI USMD_GOV_API_USMD_CUST_ETYPES.
Check in transaction MDGIMG:
Master Data Governance → General Settings → Data Modeling → Edit Entity Types and Storage Attributes → verify your ZLEG_PO and ZLEG_SO have UI Integration = Active in the 2025 customizing table.

Recommended Fix Sequence

 
Step Action
1Set breakpoint in write_data — confirm it is reached and lt_data is non-empty
2Immediately after write_data, call read_data for the same entity — confirm buffer holds the data
3Set breakpoint in UIBB's data-reading method — check whether it reads from DB or buffer
4Add NEEDS_REFRESH = abap_true and re-test
5Add iv_change_mode explicitly to write_data and re-test
6Verify ZLEG_PO / ZLEG_SO entity type UI registration in MDGIMG
The most frequently seen fix post-2025 upgrade is the combination of Cause 1 + Cause 3: the UIBB was accidentally reading from the database instead of the buffer, and NEEDS_REFRESH was returning abap_false so even the buffer read was being skipped entirely.

SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud Maintenance Calendar – Downtime Identification

The SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition maintenance calendar uses color coding and box types to distinguish between different maintenance activities. Each type carries a defined downtime window, and the calendar explicitly communicates whether a given weekend involves disruptive or potentially non-disruptive activity. [1] [2] [3]

Non-Disruptive vs. Disruptive Maintenance
Maintenance Type Calendar Indicator Downtime Required API Suspension Recommended
Global Infrastructure MaintenanceDark blue cell backgroundYes – uses full downtime windowYes
Standard Maintenance Weekend (from Sep 2026)Dark green cell backgroundYes – planned downtime for P, T, D systems once/monthYes
Online Software Change Weekend (from Sep 2026)Light green cell backgroundYes – downtime for P systems; offline change for T/DYes
Optional / Unplanned Maintenance Weekend (from Sep 2026)Light grey cell backgroundPotential – for urgent/unplanned activitiesYes (precautionary)
Software Patching – Corrections only (HFC)Green box colorYes – uses software patching downtime windowYes
Software Patching – Corrections + Continuous DeliveryBrown box colorYes – uses software patching downtime windowYes
Software Patching – HFC with Critical Fixes (xx+)Brown box colorYes – uses software patching downtime windowYes
HANA Database UpgradePurple box colorYes – uses software patching downtime windowYes
System Upgrade (Major Release)Red box colorYes – uses system upgrade downtime windowYes
Backup Weekend for Previous UpgradeGrey box colorYes – for individual systems that missed prior upgradeYes (if applicable)

[1] [2] [3]

Key Clarifications on Downtime Duration

While every maintenance window type listed above is associated with a defined downtime window, SAP's official guidance makes two important qualifications: [2] [3] [4]

  1. Systems may be released earlier than the full contractual window if the maintenance activities do not require the complete downtime period. This applies to all types of maintenance activities. [2] [3]
  2. In practice, actual downtime is often shorter than the reserved window. For example, the reserved 4-hour weekly patching window typically amounts to approximately ½ to 1 hour on average — if used at all. Similarly, major upgrade actual end-user downtime averages closer to 2 hours, despite an 8-hour reserved window. [4]

However, these are averages and not guarantees. SAP does not commit to a shorter actual downtime in the SLA.

Contractual Maintenance Windows for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

For reference, the SLA-defined windows are: [5]

Region Weekly Maintenance Window Major Upgrade Window
MENAFRI 7 pm (4 hrs)SAT 12 am (4 hrs)
APJSAT 3 pm (4 hrs)SAT 12 pm (4 hrs)
EuropeSAT 10 pm (4 hrs)SAT 7 pm (4 hrs)
AmericasSUN 4 am (4 hrs)SUN 1 am (4 hrs)
Recommendation
  • Treat all maintenance windows as potential downtime windows. The maintenance calendar does not designate any maintenance type as fully "non-disruptive" for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Every maintenance type shown in the calendar is associated with a downtime window. [2] [3]
  • Plan API suspension for the full contractual window, not just the expected average. Since systems "may be released earlier" but this is not guaranteed, integrations should be designed to handle the full reserved window gracefully (e.g., via retry logic, queuing, or scheduled suspension). [2] [3]
  • Subscribe to Cloud System Notification Subscriptions (CSNS) at https://me.sap.com/systemsprovisioning/getNotified to receive advance notifications of planned and unplanned downtimes for your specific systems. [6]
  • Monitor the SAP for Me / Cloud Availability Center (CAC) and Cloud ALM, where SAP publishes downtime window information for HFC deployments. [3]
  • For half-yearly upgrades, customers are notified approximately 6 weeks in advance via email, providing sufficient lead time to plan API suspension. [7]

Note: The specific maintenance calendar document you referenced (sap.com/documents/2021/09/...) is the authoritative source for exact dates. The color-coding legend described above is the key to interpreting whether a given weekend involves a software patch, infrastructure maintenance, upgrade, or backup activity — but all of them carry a downtime window. entry.title: Re: the Node Reference doesn‘t work in DMEE Format
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Here is the question our internal chatbot provides. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,
Henrike

#AI-Generated Content

DMEE: Why Node Reference to Aggregation Node Fails — and How to Solve It

Root Cause: DMEE Processing Sequence

This is a fundamental processing-order constraint in DMEE. The engine processes the format tree top-down and left-to-right in a single pass. The critical issue is:
  • Your SUM (Aggregation) technical node accumulates values incrementally as it iterates over payment items (line by line).
  • At the moment DMEE evaluates the condition on FPSFlg, the loop has not yet completed — the SUM node's final accumulated value is therefore not yet available (it is still zero or incomplete at that point in the processing pass).
  • A Node Reference in a condition resolves the current value of the referenced node at the instant the condition is checked — for an aggregation node still mid-loop, that value is meaningless.
This is why the Node Reference to SUM appears to do nothing or always returns 0.

The Three Valid Solutions

Solution 1 — Reference the Source Field Directly (Recommended)

This is the cleanest approach. The SAP payment program (F110 / SAPF110V) already computes the total payment amount at run time. It is available in the payment medium data structure before DMEE starts its tree traversal.
 
Scenario Field to Reference
Classic payment programREGUH-ZBTR (total house-bank amount)
Payment Medium WorkbenchThe corresponding amount field at the payment header level in your data selection
Steps in the FPSFlg condition:
  1. Open the node FPSFlg → go to the Condition tab.
  2. Set the Left-Hand Side type to Source Field (not "Node Reference").
  3. Enter the data structure/field (e.g., REGUH-ZBTR).
  4. Set the operator to < and the Right-Hand Side constant to 200000.
This bypasses the aggregation node entirely, because the source data already has the answer.

Solution 2 — Restructure the Tree Using a Pre-Aggregation Level

If you genuinely need to aggregate in DMEE (e.g., summing across multiple line items into a group total), the aggregation node must complete its loop before the node consuming its result is evaluated. This requires restructuring:
[Header Loop / Company Code Level]
   └── [SUM]  ← Aggregation node lives HERE, at the PARENT level
               ← It completes before children of this level are processed
   └── [FPSFlg]  ← Now evaluated AFTER SUM is finalized for this header
       └── [Condition: Node Reference → SUM < 200000]
The rule is: the referenced aggregation node must be a preceding sibling (or at a parent level) that closes its loop before FPSFlg is reached. If SUM and FPSFlg are inside the same repeating loop, the reference will always see an incomplete value.

Solution 3 — Use a Formula with ABAP User Exit (DMEEX)

In the Extended DMEE (DMEEX), node conditions support Formulas that can call custom function modules. You can write a short function module that:
  1. Reads the payment total from REGUH for the current payment run.
  2. Returns a flag ('X' or ' ') based on the threshold.
Then in FPSFlg's Value tab or Condition tab, reference the formula result. This gives full flexibility but requires an ABAP enhancement.
Note for S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: In-app extensibility is restricted. You can use Key User Extensibility tools, but classical ABAP user exits in DMEE are typically not available in the Public Cloud edition. Solution 1 (direct source field reference) is therefore the most practical path for your environment.

Summary

 
Approach Works in S/4HANA Cloud PE? Complexity
Source Field Reference (REGUH-ZBTR)YesLow
Tree restructure (aggregation at parent level)YesMedium
ABAP User Exit / FormulaNot in Public EditionHigh
The reason your Node Reference to SUM does not work is not a configuration mistake — it is a documented behavioral constraint: aggregation values are only finalized after their iteration completes, but node reference conditions are evaluated during (not after) the same iteration. Pointing directly to the source data field is both simpler and more reliable.
Useful SAP Help Portal references:
  • Reference Conditions (DMEE)
  • Extended Data Medium Exchange Engine (DMEEX)

#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Henrike

 

Cloud Print Manager: Multiple Paper Tray Handling in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
Recommended Approach
  • The best practice for handling multiple paper trays on a single physical printer is to create one dedicated print queue per tray in the Maintain Print Queues app. Each print queue acts as a virtual connection between the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system and a specific tray configuration on the local printer. [1]
  • You must create custom print queues (not the DEFAULT queue, which cannot be used for productive output and cannot be linked to the SAP Cloud Print Manager for Pull Integration). [2] [3]
  • Each print queue is then configured in the SAP Cloud Print Manager for Pull Integration (SAP CPM for PI), where the queue is mapped to the physical printer and its specific tray settings. [4] [5]
Tray Assignment in Cloud Print Manager

How tray selection works via PDF Settings:

  • In the SAP Cloud Print Manager for Pull Integration, each print queue has a PDF Settings configuration (available only for queues with PDF format). Within PDF Settings, the following options are relevant to tray handling: [6] [7]
    • Fit paper size: Scales the print settings in accordance with the paper size in the paper tray while preserving the aspect ratio of the original document.
    • Ignore paper size: Prevents the printer from requesting manual confirmation when a document with an invalid paper size is sent to a tray (e.g., a Letter document sent to an A4 tray).
    • Ignore print profile: When this option is deselected, CPM sends printer-specific properties (including tray selection, duplex mode, color mode, etc.) from the attached printer to the print queue in the SAP Cloud system. These properties can then be used to define print profiles for a print queue item. [6] [7] [8]

Whether tray detection is automatic or requires manual configuration:

  • Tray selection is not automatically detected from the printer. The SAP CPM for PI sends printer-specific properties to the cloud system when "Ignore print profile" is not selected — but the actual tray assignment requires deliberate configuration. [6] [8]
  • To use queue-specific print settings (including tray selection), you must:
    1. In CPM for PI PDF Settings, remove (deselect) the "Ignore print profile" option for the relevant print queue.
    2. In the SAP S/4HANA Cloud app Maintain Print Queues, select the relevant print queue and click "Manage Print Profiles" to configure queue-specific print settings, including tray selection. [8]
  • Note: Print profiles are not loaded when printing is triggered via the "Create Test Page" button in the print queue. You must trigger printing from the business application to test print profiles. [8]

For IFbA (Interactive Forms by Adobe / Adobe Forms) specifically:

  • Tray control when printing IFbA forms via CPM has a dedicated configuration path. SAP KBA 2682496 covers this scenario specifically, including the use of the ISR tray selection option in PDF Settings — however, this option is explicitly noted as being for Swiss payment form printing only and should not be used for other printing scenarios. [6] [9]
  • For Adobe Forms more broadly, tray control options include Job Profiles (SAP Notes 1743567, 2111085) and XDC file configuration, though these are more relevant to on-premise/private cloud spool-based environments. [10] [11]
Output Determination Integration
  • Output Parameter Determination (via the Output Parameter Determination app, using BRF+/BRFs business rules) is the mechanism that routes print jobs to specific print queues. [1] [2] [12]
  • In the Printer Settings determination step, the field Print Queue defines which queue a document is routed to. This can be conditioned on attributes such as:
    • Purchasing Organization
    • Document Type
    • Supplier Number
    • Company Code, and other application-specific fields [2]
  • By creating one print queue per tray and configuring Output Parameter Determination rules accordingly, you can automate routing of specific document types (e.g., invoices to tray 1, delivery notes to tray 2) to the correct queue — and therefore to the correct tray. [1] [2]
  • This is the standard best practice: Output Parameter Determination handles the routing logic (which queue), and CPM for PI + Print Profiles handle the physical tray assignment (which tray on the printer). [12] [8]
Key Considerations
  • Multiple queue options: SAP supports several configurations for assigning print users to print queues and connecting them to printers via CPM for PI — including multiple queues to one CPM server, or separate CPM servers per queue. Choose the topology that fits your infrastructure. [2]
  • Print profile activation: Queue-specific tray settings only take effect when "Ignore print profile" is deselected in CPM PDF Settings AND print profiles are maintained in the Maintain Print Queues app. If "Ignore print profile" is active, only the global CPM default settings are used. [8]
  • PDF format requirement: The PDF Settings (including tray-related options) are only available for print queues configured with PDF format. [6] [7]
  • SAP Note 2757763 covers how to print to multiple print queues or generate multiple output items — this is a useful reference for multi-queue scenarios. [2]
  • Testing: Always test print profiles by triggering output from the business application, not from the "Create Test Page" button in the print queue, as print profiles are not loaded during test page printing. [8]
  • SAP_COM_0466: The communication arrangement based on this scenario is required for CPM for PI to authenticate and poll print queues. Retrieve the System URL from this communication arrangement. [2] [13]

entry.title: Making AI Real: Black Horse One Galloping Towards New AI Opportunities
entry.content:
Here’s another nice example of Making AI Real with SAP Business AI Platform.

The reality is that many organizations aren’t yet ready to get the full benefits of artificial intelligence. In order to take a big leap forward, they have to take a small step back and make sure they have a solid platform in place.

That’s a good summary of my conversation with Daniel Göhlen, the founder of Black Horse One, a company specialized in equestrian innovation. The organization has a very atypical profile for a SAP customer: just 12 people, eight of whom are full time, and they do not use SAP ERP, only functionalities that are now part of the SAP Business AI platform, including integration and data analysis.

The company was founded as a startup, with the mission to support equestrian sports such as dressage — which the Fédération Équestre Internationale (FEI) describes as the “ultimate expression of horse training and elegance,” a complex sport where human and equine athletes compete at events all over the world, evaluated by judges and spectators in an array of categories that prize beauty, grace, and tradition.

Using SAP technology they have been able to get rid of manual, paper-based processes such as the judges’ scoring, and — more importantly — make the sport more interesting and engaging for fans. Dressage has been described as like judging ice skating competitions, but with riders and their horses. There’s the same notion of a set of figures that have to be completed, with scoring individual parts of the routine for difficulty and overall artistry.

Black Horse One started their journey by providing a small group of officials with iPads and an application that allowed them to score the competitions more easily. But now they cover many different aspects of the sport, with two to three million people now using the software on a regular basis. The ability to update, calculate, and share information in real time, during the competitions, was a key element in the organization’s choice of the SAP platform.

Their challenges have been ones that will be familiar to anybody reading this — such as unified and harmonized data. In their case, that means being able to use elements of the platform such as SAP Business Data Cloud to track if a horse moves from one federation to another, even though that means they end up with a different identifier. For example, the owners may live in a border region, competing in both Germany and the Netherlands, with different IDs. Being able to track the full horse history is important, especially for things like tracking horse welfare — the equestrian equivalent of predictive maintenance, making sure that the “equipment” is getting all of the care it deserves.

So where does AI come in? Daniel notes that Black Horse One is still in the early stages of exploring the “tremendous” potential of AI, but because his organization has one of the largest data set within the equestrian sphere, there are some big opportunities. For example training is obviously a key focus, and so they have created an application that tracks and extracts everything that trainers need track performance.

And Black Horse One is using AI to make a direct difference to the fan experience. For example, at smaller venues, there often isn’t a dedicated, knowledgeable announcer for the event. The organization offers organizers the possibility of AI announcers, complete with the voices of well-known stars of the industry, who give real-time results and statistics from the platform in order to keep the crowds engaged and help recreate the bigger-venue feel.

Daniel finished up our session with a message for other small organizations that might hesitate to use a product like SAP: “Even if you are such a small company, give it a shot. I can really recommend it ... for our mission critical processes, SAP is the way to go and we'll definitely stick with it."

To learn more about how Black Horse One brought digital transformation to the tradition-bound world of equestrian sports, check out the links below, and see the full series of SAP Customer Conversations: Better Together episodes for more best practices and lessons learned.

  • My official SAP News article
  • Thought leadership podcast: Göhlen, CEO of Black Horse One, talks with Tamara McCleary, CEO of Thulium, to share his motivation and journey merging tradition with technology to transform equestrian events, improving the sport and the sporting experience for athletes and audiences and winning over even the most traditional participants.
  • Practitioners’ video: Göhlen talks with me about what it took and the technologies that have resulted in a suite of applications that revolutionized the dressage world.

entry.title: From incident to insight: How SAP RootMap transforms RCA creation
entry.content:
The process to figure out what went wrong is called a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and is critical to both keeping customers informed and to creating lessons learned reports so SAP can work to prevent the next failure. The manual process is time-consuming. Investigators must manually pull together records, notes, and timelines from multiple sources, a process that takes an average of 15 hours per incident when accounting for cross-team coordination, research, validation, and final findings approval.

SAP RootMap cuts that time to under two minutes for the initial RCA draft. The tool automatically retrieves incident records from SAP's internal systems and uses AI to produce a structured report. Instead of spending hours collecting data, problem managers start with a ready-made summary and spend their time reviewing, refining, and approving the findings.

entry.title: Model company for SAP cloud solutions: Helping consultants make better Fit-to-Standard decisions
entry.content:
Part 3 of the blog series on model company for SAP cloud solutions

 

Introduction

 

Anyone who has prepared a Fit-to-Standard workshop knows how much work goes into getting ready. You need a system that runs, a relevant business scenario, and data that make sense to the customer. Without these, it is easy for the discussion to stay at the level of slides and assumptions.

Model company for SAP cloud solutions can help. It provides preconfigured reference content for available industries and lines of business. Once this content is deployed, consultants can demonstrate working SAP S/4HANA processes, supported by process flow diagrams and test materials. This makes it easier to prepare workshops around real business questions.

Part 1 of this series explained what a model company is. Part 2 looked at it from an architect’s perspective. This article focuses on what consultants can do with it: prepare workshops, assess how standard processes meet customer needs, identify justified requirements and turn business decisions into clear next steps for implementation.

 

The Consultant’s Challenge: From Preparation to Value

 

Before a workshop can start, someone must get the groundwork right: set up relevant processes, prepare master and transactional data, test the scenarios, and make sure everything runs smoothly. Much of this work is repeated from one project to the next. If too much time goes into setup, there is less time to discuss what the business needs.

Model company can reduce this effort by providing a preconfigured reference system. It does not remove the need to be prepared.  Consultants still need to check whether the right industry and country scope is available, whether the environment is ready, and which of the delivered scenarios are most relevant to the business discussions. The difference is that they can spend more time deciding what to validate with the business and less time setting up examples.

 

What consultants can use in model company

 

Depending on the available industry and line-of-business content, consultants can use:

  • Working process scenarios: Preconfigured end-to-end business processes that can be run and demonstrated in the reference environment.
  • Business data: Sample master data that enables consultants to run business scenarios, create transactions, and experience how the processes work in practice.
  • Process and project materials: Process flow diagrams available for download or as SAP Signavio process models for further adaption, complemented by SAP Cloud ALM scope materials, for those using SAP Cloud ALM, to support workshops and follow-up activities.
  • Test materials: Available test scripts to guide scenario execution and support testing activities in later project phases. Automated tests are not available for every scenario.

Not every industry has the same content. Check out the current industry and line-of-business dashboard, linked from Part 1, before planning a workshop around a specific scenario.

 

Show & tell in practice: from demonstration to decision

 

A Show & Tell session makes Fit-to-Standard tangible. In a procure-to-pay workshop, the consultant checks the relevant model company scenario, reference environment and data before guiding business users through the live process e.g.:

  • Create a purchase requisition
  • Turn it into a purchase order
  • Receive the goods
  • Process the supplier invoice
  • Make the payment

The goal is to discuss business needs alongside the demonstration and walkthrough. The consultant pauses at key steps, such as purchase order approval, to explore the customer's controls within the working process. This gives business users a real sense of their processes in practice and the ability to link visuals with concepts, ultimately speeding up decision-making and reducing the risk of future changes.

Figure 1. A live procure-to-pay process anchors the Show & Tell discussion.

A purchasing manager says, “We need three approval levels before a purchase order can be released.” The consultant asks why. Is this a legal or internal control requirement? What risk does it address? Or is it an inherited practice?

Compare the requirements with the live process and any supported configuration options. The discussion may lead to three outcomes:

  • Standard process meets the need: No change is required.
  • Configuration can meet the need: A supported configuration option should be checked against the customer’s requirements.
  • Further assessment is needed: A justified exception needs a clear reason, an owner, and a decision once the impact is understood.

For example, the team could confirm standard purchase order creation, ask the consultant to verify supported approval configuration, and involve the architect if an external approval is justified. Give each open item to the owner and take the next step. This prevents every difference from the current system from becoming a deviation. 

 

Before, during and after the workshop

Before: prepare the right questions

Confirm the required industry content and access to a provisioned model company reference environment. Check business roles and sample data, rehearse the selected scenario from end to end, and agree which decisions the Show & Tell must support. For scope and request instructions, see SAP Note 3631601.

During: work through the business decisions

Introduce the business context, then run the process live and pause where important decisions arise. Ask whether each step supports what the business needs. Separate what fits, what may need configuration and what needs further assessment. For open items, record why they matter, who will follow up, and when a decision is expected. SAP Cloud ALM can support this by capturing requirements, decisions and follow-up activities directly against the model company scope elements already available in the tool. Your role is to guide a useful discussion, not simply write down every difference.

After: turn decisions into next steps

Summarize the agreed process scope, open configuration questions, justified requirements, and any impact on testing. If the project uses SAP Signavio and SAP Cloud ALM, their process models and project materials can help teams record and track the outcomes. With model company scope elements already available in SAP Cloud ALM, teams can build on this foundation to capture workshop decisions, requirements, and follow-up activities.

A future deep-dive article will show how to access and prepare a model company environment, select a scenario and run a Show & Tell session from setup through follow-up.

 

How model company supports SAP Activate

 

Model company is especially useful when preparing workshops and validating processes during Explore. Its content and supporting materials can also help in later phases. SAP Activate has six phases: Discover, Prepare, Explore, Realize, Deploy and Run. The illustration below focuses on the work consultants do from Prepare onward and groups Deploy and Run together.

One important point: model company serve as a reference for the project. It is not necessarily the environment used to build or run the customer’s solution.

  • Prepare: Access or set up the available model company reference, then choose the processes, data and materials needed for the customer’s workshops.
  • Explore: Demonstrate live end-to-end scenarios, check whether they meet business needs and document the decisions and justify requirements that will guide the implementation.
  • Realize: Apply the agreed decisions in the customer implementation environment. Use relevant reference content and available test materials to support configuration, extensions, and testing.
  • Deploy and Run: Use the process knowledge, documented decisions and applicable test assets to help with go-live preparation, handover and later improvements.

Figure 2. How consultants can use model company during the implementation journey (simplified view).

Keeping the core clean in day-to-day work

 

Clean core is not only an architecture topic. Consultants influence it whenever they accept a requirement, choose a configuration option or propose an extension. Model company offers a reference aligned with clean-core principles, but the customer solution still needs to be designed and built accordingly.

First, check whether the business needs can be met through the standard process or supported configuration. If an extension is justified, discuss the options with the architect and follow the approach supported for the customer solution. This may include key-user, developer/on-stack or side-by-side extensibility, using released interfaces and APIs where required. Record why the decision was made and how it will be tested, so the teams who take over can understand and maintain it.

 

Working with architects

 

Consultants and architects need to work from the same process decisions, but their responsibilities are different. Architects set the overall design and technical boundaries. Consultants work with business users to confirm which processes fit and turn those decisions into configuration, requirements and tests for the customer environment. Keeping process models and decisions up to date helps both roles stay aligned.

 

Conclusion: better decisions, not just faster preparation

 

For consultants, the biggest advantage is not simply having access to a preconfigured system. It can show a real process, question assumptions, and distinguish genuine business requirements from habits carried over from the previous system.

At your next Fit-to-Standard workshop, consider starting with one relevant end-to-end scenario from the available model company content. Show what already works, discuss any exceptions, and document the decisions needed for the next stage of the project. That is where the preparation starts to pay off.

In your Fit-to-Standard workshops, what takes the most effort:

  • preparing realistic scenarios
  • moving the discussion away from old customizations
  • turning workshop decisions into clear requirements? 

I would be interested to hear what has worked for you. Share your experience in the comments.

 

More from this series

 

Part 1 — Model company for SAP cloud solutions: Your Fast Track to Fit-to-Standard

Part 2 — Model company for SAP cloud solutions for Architects: From Target Architecture to an Executable Baseline

Next in the series: the partner perspective, a closer look at the content and supporting tools, and articles about individual industries as more content becomes available.

To explore what is available, see the industry and line-of-business dashboard linked in Part 1. For scope and request instructions, see SAP Note 3631601. For questions, email modelcompany@sap.com.

About the author: Erik Rahm is Program Manager for model company for SAP cloud solutions at SAP, bringing 30+ years of experience in SAP and enterprise transformation.

entry.title: Re: Missing Profit Center in G/L Line Items for Year-End...
entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

 

This is a well-known and documented behavior in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Here is a structured explanation based on official SAP documentation and KBAs found.

Why Profit Center is Missing from Document Type CL Line Items

The Italian year-end closing/opening program ("Schedule Post Closing and Opening Balances", app F6182, underlying program FAGL_YEC_POSTINGS with Italy variant FAGL_IT_01) is a country-specific statutory requirement — used in Italy, Turkey, Romania, and Colombia — that creates accounting documents to zero out all account balances and reopen them in the new fiscal year. Source: SAP KBA 3506004

The program works at the aggregate account balance level, not at the analytical dimension level. This means it sums up the net balance of each G/L account across all profit centers and generates one closing entry and one opening entry per account. It does not carry through the Profit Center dimension from the individual underlying line items.

This behaviour is also rooted in how Document Type CL is classified in Document Splitting. According to SAP documentation, CL is assigned to business transaction 0000 = "Unspecified Posting", which covers "all business processes that have complete account assignments and therefore do not need to be split" — such as CO or MM postings. This means the document splitting engine does not apply active splitting rules to CL documents. If the Profit Center is not populated in the source data fed into the closing program, the resulting CL line items will show a blank Profit Center. Source: SAP Help – Document Types Used in Document Splitting, Unspecified Posting 0000

Why the Trial Balance Shows the Correct Profit Center

The Trial Balance app (F0996) derives its opening balances from ACDOCA balance data, including balance carryforward period 000 entries, which are generated by the separate "Carry Forward Balances" step and do retain Profit Center detail. The CL document is a distinct statutory/audit posting that exists in parallel.

Importantly, SAP KBA 3506004 explicitly states that the cloud version of Trial Balance (F0996) does not actually support including closing/opening year-end postings. What you see as correct in the Trial Balance is the carryforward balance, not the CL document content. For statutory reporting that includes the CL postings, SAP recommends:

  • App F0707A – Display G/L Account Balances
  • App W0161 – Balance Sheet/Income Statement – Multidimensional

How to Address the Issue Going Forward

There is no single configuration switch that retroactively fixes the missing Profit Center in already-generated CL documents. The approaches below apply to future year-end runs.

Option 1 – Document Splitting: Zero-Balance Characteristic for Profit Center

If Profit Center is configured as a "Zero Balance" splitting characteristic, the document splitting engine generates additional clearing line items to ensure each profit center balances to zero — even in CL documents. This is the architecturally correct solution for reporting a balance sheet per profit center in S/4HANA.

Configuration path (via Configure Your Solution):

Financial Accounting → General Ledger Accounting → Business Transactions → Document Splitting → Define Document Splitting Characteristics for General Ledger Accounting

Set the Profit Center field to "Zero Balance". Be aware that activating or changing this characteristic after go-live requires careful handling of open items and opening balances — see KBA 3638627 for the detailed procedure. In S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, changes to document splitting characteristics may require involvement of your SAP Product Expert, since the system restricts changes once production postings exist. Source: SAP Help – Document Splitting Characteristics

Option 2 – Open an SAP Support Incident

Given that this is a documented country-specific program and you have confirmed the Profit Center is missing from the physical CL document, this may qualify as a defect or a known gap. SAP KBA 3506004 is the directly relevant note for your scenario. Reference it when opening an incident, and ask specifically whether there is an SAP correction or configuration option for the Italian variant (FAGL_IT_01) to disaggregate postings by Profit Center.

Option 3 – Reporting Workaround (immediate relief)

For regulatory reporting that currently relies on F2217 for CL documents, switch to the apps SAP explicitly supports for this use case:

  • F0707A – Display G/L Account Balances (includes closing/opening postings)
  • W0161 – Balance Sheet/Income Statement – Multidimensional

These apps source their data from the ACDOCA balance layer where Profit Center is populated, rather than from the physical CL document line items.

Summary

Aspect Explanation

Root causeItalian closing/opening program aggregates balances per G/L account; Doc Type CL uses business transaction 0000 (no splitting required)
Trial Balance discrepancyTrial Balance reads ACDOCA carryforward data (period 000), not the CL physical document
Structural fixActivate Profit Center as a Zero-Balance characteristic in Document Splitting
Immediate workaroundUse F0707A or W0161 instead of F2217 for statutory reporting of closing/opening postings
SAP referenceKBA 3506004, KBA 3638627

Sources: SAP KBA 3506004 | SAP Help – Document Splitting (Cloud) | Document Types in Document Splitting | Document Splitting Characteristics

entry.title: Re: SAP Transportation management public cloud, packaging
entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

 

Let me lay out a clear picture of what standard SAP offers and where the real boundaries are.

The Core Problem

In standard SAP, the material master holds one NLQ conversion per product/UoM combination (e.g., 1 EPL = 500 KG). Since every customer gets a custom pallet with a different KG value but the same UoM (EPL), there is no native "customer-specific UoM conversion" in either the material master or the NLQ configuration table. SAP's NLQ determination is product-oriented, not customer-oriented.

What SAP Standard Actually Offers

Here are the real options, ranked by practicality for your case:

Option 1 -- "Define Normalized Quantity" App (Closest to Your Need)

SAP documentation (help.sap.com) confirms the system uses this priority logic:

  1. First: look up the product + UoM in the Define Normalized Quantity app (individual NLQ per product/reference product)
  2. Second: fall back to the material master alternative UoM conversion

The "Define Normalized Quantity" app allows you to define an NLQ value per product and UoM, independently of the material master. However, this is still product-level -- there is no customer dimension in this table. So this alone does not solve the customer-specific pallet weight requirement.

Option 2 -- Separate Material Codes per Customer

You already identified this. It is the most straightforward standard approach: create one material (e.g., MAT-EPL-CUSTA, MAT-EPL-CUSTB) per customer variant, each with its own EPL-to-KG conversion in the material master. The sales order item would reference the customer-specific material.

Pros: fully standard, no workarounds
Cons: master data explosion, maintenance burden, potential confusion on the sales side

Option 3 -- Use Gross Weight Directly (Bypass NLQ for Weight)

This approach reframes the problem. Instead of relying on the EPL-to-KG conversion for weight tracking in the Transportation Cockpit, you configure the freight unit to use gross weight directly from the sales order item as the weight quantity. The NLQ (pallet count) stays as-is since pallet count does not vary by customer -- only the KG per pallet does.

If the sales order item carries the correct gross weight for the material quantity ordered (which it typically does if the material master has accurate per-EA or per-KG weight data), then:

  • The Transportation Cockpit shows correct weight utilization from the gross weight field
  • The pallet count (EPL) continues to come from the NLQ conversion

This decouples weight accuracy from the NLQ conversion, which is what you actually want. The weight shown in the cockpit would then be correct for each customer without needing customer-specific pallet conversions.

This is worth examining closely: the issue may specifically be that you are using EPL as the weight-carrying quantity. If the weight flows correctly from product net weight x quantity ordered, you may not need the EPL-to-KG conversion to be customer-specific at all.

Option 4 -- Material Freight Groups as a Differentiator

SAP documentation confirms that the material freight group (assigned in the material master under Sales/General Plant Data and transferred to the freight unit item) can be used as a differentiating input in freight unit building rules. However, material freight groups also do not carry a customer dimension -- they are still product-level.

This option could make sense combined with Option 2 (different material per customer) to keep freight unit building rules clean.

Option 5 -- Condition-Based Freight Unit Building Rules

SAP documents that freight unit building rules can be selected via a condition in the logistics integration profile. This means different FUBR can apply to different ship-to parties. However, the FUBR controls splitting logic and critical quantities -- it does not change the NLQ-to-KG conversion factor per customer. So this does not directly solve the weight conversion problem either.

What Is Not Available in Standard (Cloud Public Edition)

  • No customer-specific UoM conversion table for NLQ (not in standard TM configuration)
  • No BAdI for custom NLQ determination in Cloud Public Edition (BAdI extensibility is more restricted than Private Edition/on-premise)
  • No "customer material info record" influence on TM NLQ values

My Practical Recommendation

Given your constraints (no EWM, consolidation on sales order, no delivery-based FU building), the most viable standard approach is a combination of Options 3 and 2:

  1. First, check whether configuring the freight unit to use gross weight from the sales order (rather than deriving weight via EPL-to-KG) already gives you correct weight utilization in the Transportation Cockpit. If the order item gross weight is accurate per customer (because the ordered quantity and per-unit weight are correct), this may be enough without any customer-specific pallet conversion.

  2. If you genuinely need the EPL quantity to reflect customer-specific KG (e.g., for pallet-space-based charge calculation), then separate material codes per customer remains the only fully clean standard path. This is not ideal, but it is what SAP's architecture provides for this level of granularity.

The "custom conversion table" idea (your second option) would require extensibility that is not available in Cloud Public Edition standard, so it falls outside the scope of staying in SAP Standard.

Sources:

  • Creation and Editing of Freight Units: help.sap.com
  • Use of Number of Pallet Spaces and Loading Meters: help.sap.com
  • TM in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2308 (SAP Community blog): community.sap.com
  • Configuring Transportation Master Data (SAP Learning): learning.sap.com

entry.title: Re: Cxml punchout catalog for purchase requisition in SAP...
entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

This is an important distinction that the SAP documentation makes clearly. Here is what you need to know.

Short Answer

Yes, you can create a PR directly from a supplier catalog in F2229 -- but the punchout mechanism in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is OCI-based, not cXML-based. If your supplier speaks cXML for punchout, there is a fundamental protocol mismatch to address.

How Punchout Works in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (without Ariba)

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition supports punchout catalogs natively through the Open Catalog Interface (OCI 4.0/5.0) -- not through cXML. The setup is done in the "Settings for Web Services" app (F1994), with no Ariba license required.

The flow in F2229 is:

  1. The buyer opens F2229 and selects "Add from External Catalog."
  2. SAP sends an OCI request to the supplier's punchout URL.
  3. The buyer shops on the supplier's site and adds items to the cart.
  4. The supplier's site returns the cart data back to SAP via the OCI HOOK_URL.
  5. Items are populated directly into the Purchase Requisition.

The cXML Problem

This is the core issue for your scenario. SAP's own community documentation states explicitly:

"In Public Cloud, punchout is an OCI scenario, not a cXML-based scenario." Source

cXML-based punchout (using PunchOutSetupRequest / PunchOutSetupResponse / PunchOutOrderMessage) is the protocol used by SAP Ariba Buying and SAP Business Network -- not by native S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Without an Ariba license or Ariba Buying integration, SAP has no cXML punchout engine to handle the supplier's cXML messages.

Your Options

Option Description Ariba needed?

OCI punchout (native)Configure the supplier catalog in "Settings for Web Services" using OCI. The supplier must support OCI in addition to or instead of cXML.No
cXML punchout via Ariba BuyingUse SAP Ariba Buying (Base Edition) as the catalog intermediary, which handles the cXML protocol.Yes
Supplier adapts to OCIAsk the supplier whether their punchout site also supports OCI return (many do, as OCI is widely supported).No

Recommended Path (without Ariba)

Check with your supplier whether their catalog site supports OCI 4.0 return in addition to cXML. Many suppliers who support cXML punchout also support OCI, since OCI is the SAP-native protocol. If they do, you can configure the punchout directly in:

  • App: "Settings for Web Services" (F1994)
  • Define the catalog URL (supplier's punchout landing URL)
  • Set HOOK_URL to blank (type: Return URL -- SAP calculates it at runtime)
  • Assign the catalog to the relevant purchasing org/plant

The items selected on the supplier's site will then be returned directly into the F2229 PR.

Prerequisites for Native OCI Punchout Setup

  • Business role with access to "Settings for Web Services" (key user role required)
  • Supplier must support OCI 4.0 (or OCI 5.0, which requires a Communication Arrangement in addition)
  • Catalog URL from the supplier
  • Optional: BAdI MMPUR_OCI_TO_DRAFT_ITM_MAPPING for custom field mapping on item return

Sources:

  • Settings for Web Services -- SAP Help
  • OCI PunchOut catalog does not open -- SAP Note 3776256
  • Maintaining HOOK_URL -- SAP Note 3551234
  • cXML for service requisitions lines -- SAP Community
  • Setup of Punch-out Catalogs -- SAP Community Blog

The Monitor Value Chains app (App ID: F4854) not appearing in IAM when maintaining business users is a known authorization setup gap. Activating scope item 5MQ alone does not automatically make the app available in IAM -- the required business catalog must also be assigned to the business role.

Prerequisites

Setup Steps
