entry.title: Re: SII Spain: error 3019 when reversing an invoice from...
entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Here is a structured summary of what is known about this scenario and your three questions.

Background: Why Error 3019 Occurs

The AEAT validates that the <PeriodoLiquidacion> (year + month) in a deregistration request matches the period of the last prior movement for that invoice. When SAP sends the reversal as a deregistration but stamps it with period B's tax reporting date, the AEAT rejects it with error 3019: "El Ejercicio y Periodo del PeriodoLiquidacion deben coincidir con el último movimiento anterior."

This is a structural constraint on the deregistration message type itself, not a SAP limitation. The AEAT deregistration flow is designed to cancel a specific prior registration, so it must carry the same period reference.

Your Three Questions

1. How have others solved error 3019 in this cross-period scenario?

No documented accepted answer exists on the SAP Community thread you posted (as of the search results available). The thread is recent (October 2026) and still open. From what the documentation and community sources reveal, the root cause is confirmed: you cannot change the tax reporting date to period B on a deregistration-type eDocument without triggering error 3019. The only paths that avoid the error are either:

  • Keep the deregistration pointing at period A (the original period), which is what the AEAT structurally requires for a "baja", or
  • Stop using the deregistration flow altogether for this case and send a new invoice-type eDocument instead.

There is no documented SAP note or workaround that patches error 3019 for cross-period supplier invoice reversals in Public Edition.

2. Does sending the reversal as a new invoice (F1/R1) with the current period's tax reporting date avoid the error in practice?

Based on the SAP documentation on date determination, yes -- this is the documented alternative. SAP distinguishes two reversal paths:

  • "Errors (Reversals) SII as Deregistration": uses the original document's tax reporting date. This triggers error 3019 if you try to force it into a different period.
  • "Errors (Reversals) SII as Negative Invoice": uses the reversal document's billing/posting date, so the eDocument picks up period B's date.

Configuration activity 102954 option "Send new invoice with type F1/F2/R1/R1S/R2/R2S/R3/R3S" maps to the negative invoice path. When configured this way, SAP creates a new incoming invoice eDocument (not a deregistration) with a negative amount and the reversal document's tax reporting date. This should submit to period B without triggering error 3019, because the AEAT period consistency check applies to deregistrations, not to new invoice registrations.

Important caveats:

  • This means the original registration in period A is never cancelled in the SII. Period A's books at the AEAT will still show the original invoice. Only period B will show the offsetting negative entry. Whether the customer's tax advisor and the AEAT accept this approach is a question for their tax counsel, not something the standard documentation resolves.
  • F1 is a normal invoice type; R1 is a correction invoice (error based on articles 80.1, 80.2, 80.6 LIVA). For received invoices reversed for accounting reasons rather than for a genuine VAT correction, the appropriate invoice type classification would need to be confirmed with the customer's tax advisor.

3. Is there a standard way to send deregistration for same-period reversals and an opposite-sign entry for cross-period reversals?

No. Configuration activity 102954 is fixed per company code and document type. SAP standard does not provide a dynamic rule that branches between deregistration (same period) and new negative invoice (different period) based on a runtime comparison of the original invoice's period against the current period.

There is also no BAdI documented for Spain incoming invoice reversal handling in Public Edition that would let you implement this logic. (The EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD~CHANGE_INVOICE_TYPE BAdI that exists in the eDocument framework is documented as available only for France at the time of writing.)

Practical Options to Consider

Given the above, the realistic options are:

Option A -- Configure "Send new invoice" (F1/R1) globally for the relevant document type. This avoids error 3019 in both same-period and cross-period scenarios. The trade-off is that same-period reversals will also not generate a deregistration, so the original entry in period A remains in the AEAT books, offset by a new negative entry. For many customers this is acceptable, but it needs sign-off from the tax team.

Option B -- Keep the deregistration configuration and manually adjust the tax reporting date on the reversal back to period A before generating the eDocument. This points the baja at the closed period, which is what the AEAT expects. The customer's concern about "modifying a filed period" is a business policy concern rather than an AEAT rule -- the baja cancels the prior registration entry; it does not reopen or amend the VAT return. This should be clarified with the customer's tax advisor.

Option C -- Open a support incident with SAP (component FI-LOC-FI-ES) describing the cross-period scenario. Given the thread has no accepted answer and the gap appears to be a product limitation, SAP support can confirm whether a fix or BAdI is planned.

Sources:

  • SII Spain error 3019 - SAP Community thread
  • Date Determination in Sales - SAP Help Portal
  • Configuration Options for SII for VAT - SAP Help Portal
  • Tax Reporting Date and Tax Fulfillment Date - SAP Help Portal
  • AEAT SII FAQs v1.1 - Agencia Tributaria

entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

This is a well-known pain point in SAP Asset Management, and you're right that measurement documents are not designed for this use case. Here's an overview of the approaches available in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, from the most standard to more advanced options.

The Core Problem

Measurement documents are designed for recurring counter or meter readings (runtime hours, km, cycles), not for tracking discrete upgrade events across a fleet of equipment. Using them for upgrade tracking forces you to create a measuring point per upgrade type per equipment item, which is exactly the scalability issue you're describing.

Recommended Approaches

1. Improvement Maintenance Orders (Order Type YA03)

This is the most purpose-fit standard option. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition includes a dedicated maintenance type called "Improvement Maintenance" specifically for upgrade and enhancement activities on technical objects.

  • Create one maintenance order per upgrade per equipment item
  • Track planning, execution, costs, labor, and materials through the standard maintenance lifecycle (notification -> order -> confirmation -> completion)
  • The order is linked to the equipment master and builds a complete maintenance history
  • Use the "Find Maintenance Orders" app (F2173) to search and filter across all 50 equipment items at once by order type, status, dates, and equipment
  • Mass editing of order details across multiple orders is supported

The key advantage: the order and its history are tied to the equipment record, so you get a full audit trail without defining anything at the measuring point level.

Source: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition -- Asset Management

2. Equipment Classification with Characteristics

For tracking the upgrade state of each equipment item (e.g., firmware version, hardware revision level, last upgrade date), you can use the classification framework:

  • Assign an equipment class to all 50 pieces of equipment
  • Define characteristics on that class (e.g., "Current Firmware Version", "Upgrade Status", "Last Upgrade Date")
  • Update characteristic values as upgrades are performed
  • The Equipment API (API_EQUIPMENT_CLASSIFICATION_SRV) supports mass read, create, and update of these values

One known limitation: there is currently no native mass-assignment template for class characteristics in the standard UI. The workaround is to use the classification API for bulk updates or to extend the equipment with Custom Fields (see below).

Source: Equipment Class Characteristics API -- SAP Help Portal

3. Custom Fields on Equipment Master

Via the Key User Extensibility app ("Custom Fields"), you can add user-defined fields directly to the equipment master record -- for example, "Upgrade Version", "Upgrade Status" (dropdown), or "Last Upgraded On" (date field).

  • These fields persist across system upgrades and are not overwritten by SAP release updates
  • They can be enabled for UIs, reports, APIs, and free-text search
  • You can report across all 50 equipment items in a single list using these fields
  • No per-equipment configuration is needed -- the field exists at the master data level for the whole object type

This is a lower-effort approach than classification if you only need a handful of status fields rather than a full characteristic hierarchy.

Source: Extensibility in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

4. Performance Monitoring: SAP Asset Performance Management (APM)

If your requirement extends beyond tracking that an upgrade happened to monitoring asset health and performance after each upgrade, SAP Asset Performance Management is the dedicated product for this:

  • Connects to your S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition back end as the EAM source
  • Surfaces equipment master data, maintenance history, notifications, and measuring point data
  • Supports reliability analysis, failure mode tracking, and KPI monitoring per equipment
  • Requires S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2202 or higher as the back end

Source: SAP Asset Performance Management -- Minimum Release Requirements

5. Analytics: Plant Maintenance Analysis in SAP Analytics Cloud

For a reporting and monitoring layer across all 50 equipment items, SAP Analytics Cloud includes pre-built content for Enterprise Asset Management:

  • Analyzes maintenance orders (including improvement orders), notifications, costs, activities, and technical objects
  • Can be sliced by plant, equipment class, order type, and status
  • Provides a cross-equipment view without manual aggregation

Source: Enterprise Asset Management -- Plant Maintenance Analysis for SAP S/4HANA

Recommended End-to-End Design

Layer Tool Purpose

Upgrade executionImprovement Maintenance Orders (YA03)Plan, track, and complete each upgrade; build history
Upgrade stateCustom Fields or Classification CharacteristicsRecord current version / status on equipment master
Cross-fleet visibilityFind Maintenance Orders app + Custom Fields listMonitor all 50 items in one view
Performance monitoringSAP Asset Performance Management (if licensed)Post-upgrade health and reliability trending
ReportingSAP Analytics Cloud EAM contentManagement dashboards and KPI tracking

The most pragmatic starting point is Improvement Maintenance Orders combined with a small set of Custom Fields on the equipment master. This avoids the per-equipment measuring point overhead and gives you a scalable, history-preserving record for each upgrade across your entire fleet.

here is what the official documentation and SAP support content say about this.

Why Document PRT Work Instructions Do Not Transfer from S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP Digital Manufacturing

This is a confirmed product limitation, documented in SAP Knowledge Base Article 3676619.

The KBA explicitly states:

"Work instructions (Document PRTs) assigned to operations in the routing of a production order are not integrated from S/4HANA Public Cloud to SAP Digital Manufacturing."

This is not a configuration issue you can resolve, it is a deliberate scope difference between S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and ERP/on-premise scenarios.

Root Cause

The integration between S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Digital Manufacturing supports only a subset of PRT types for transfer via production orders. According to the SAP Digital Manufacturing Integration Guide:

  • Material PRTs: supported (production order transfer)
  • Equipment PRTs: supported (via Equipment/Tool sync)
  • Document PRTs: not supported in the S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition integration path

The DM Tool Management integration recognizes only Equipment and Material as tool types in its Manage Tools app. There is no corresponding concept for a Document PRT as a "tool" in DM.

Additionally, the Document Info Record (DIR) transfer path for work instructions is described in the SAP DM integration guide under Configuring a Production Order with Document Info Records, but that path applies to SAP ERP 6.0 EHP6 or higher (on-premise), not to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

What You Can Do Instead

There is a separate KBA, 3633442, that covers how to open a work instruction (PRT document) in the SAP DM POD. The approach there is to create the PRT document and work instruction directly in SAP Digital Manufacturing rather than transferring it from the ERP side.

For work instructions originating in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the practical alternatives are:

  1. Maintain work instructions natively in SAP Digital Manufacturing (decoupled from the ERP routing).
  2. Use the routing transfer path and manually attach work instructions to the operation in DM after the routing arrives.
  3. Check the Technical Integration page for whether "Work Instruction (DMS Document) Integration" as a communication arrangement covers your specific scenario -- but note this is described for ERP, not S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Source: SAP KBA 3676619 | SAP DM Integration Guide | SAP DM Integration Overview

#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

here is a consolidated answer to each of your four points, based on SAP Help Portal documentation and official SAP KBA/Community sources.

Extensibility of the Outgoing Check Form in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

1. Can custom fields be added to the check form via the Display function?

No. The outgoing check form (technical name: FIN_FO_PAYM_CHECK_US, data source: FDP_FFO_PAYM_CHECK_SRV) is not released for key-user extensibility in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The underlying FDP data source is not available for extension. As a result, it is not possible to add new custom fields (YY1*/ZZ* fields) to the check form data model using the Custom Fields app.

This is explicitly confirmed in:

  • SAP Community thread (January 2026): Business Context to Outgoing Checks (FIN_FO_PAYM_CHECK_US)
  • SAP KBA 3654275 (October 2025): Display Company Code Address in Check Form

2. Is there a BAdI, Custom Logic option, or form enhancement framework available?

No BAdI or Custom Logic implementation is available for populating customer-specific fields in the outgoing check form payload. Specifically:

  • No business context is exposed for FIN_FO_PAYM_CHECK_US in the Custom Fields app.
  • No Custom Logic BAdI exists to inject data into the FDP_FFO_PAYM_CHECK_SRV data source.
  • This is in contrast to other finance output forms (such as Payment Advice), where SAP explicitly supports this extensibility pattern.

3. What extensibility is available for the check form?

The only supported customization is a layout-level modification of the form template itself, using the Maintain Form Templates app. This does not enable new data fields, but allows visual/layout adjustments to existing data:

Steps:

  1. Open the Maintain Form Templates app.
  2. Search for the standard template (e.g., FIN_FO_PAYM_CHECK_US for the US).
  3. Download the XDP file and edit it using Adobe LiveCycle Designer (version 10.4 or higher, provided by SAP).
  4. Upload the modified template as a new custom template.
  5. Assign the custom template in the Output Parameter Determination app under "Outgoing Checks."

Important constraint: Layout customization only allows rearranging or restyling the existing fields already available in the standard data payload. It does not make additional custom data fields available, since the data source cannot be extended.

Reference: Configuring the Output for Outgoing Checks | SAP Blog: Customize Content Form for Outgoing Check

4. Confirmation: is this a fixed SAP standard output?

Yes. The outgoing check form (FIN_FO_PAYM_CHECK_US and its country equivalents) is a fixed SAP standard output form in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Custom field extensibility through the Custom Fields and Logic app is not supported for this form. The data model behind the check form cannot be enhanced via standard key-user extensibility tools.

Recommended Alternative: Payment Advice Form

If the business requirement is to communicate additional customer-specific information to the payee, SAP recommends using the Payment Advice form, which does support full key-user extensibility:

  • Custom fields can be created via the Custom Fields app using the business context "Finance: Payment Advice."
  • Two BAdIs are available for populating custom fields:
    • FBL_PAYM_ADV_PRINT_HEADER: for header-level custom fields
    • FBL_PAYM_ADV_PRINT_ITEM: for item-level custom fields
  • Custom fields can then be bound to the payment advice form template.

Reference: Adding Custom Fields to Payment Advice Forms (SAP Help Portal)

Correct link: Adding Custom Fields to Payment Advice Forms

BAdI / Custom Logic for check form dataNot available

entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Henrike

Automatic Batch Determination with FEFO in EWM Outbound Delivery Picking

This is a how-to/setup response for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with embedded EWM.

A key architectural point first: when the storage location is EWM-managed, EWM is the "upper system" for batch determination — not the S/4HANA delivery. S/4HANA sends only the batch selection criteria to EWM; EWM then assigns the actual batch during warehouse task/picking creation, and writes it back to the outbound delivery. This is why pure SD-side automatic batch determination will not work in this scenario. Source

Prerequisites

  • EWM integration is active (business function LE — Extended Warehouse Management Integration enabled). Source
  • The warehouse is configured as an ERP warehouse with EWM.
  • The material is batch-managed (batch management indicator set in Material Master).
  • Automatic batch determination is activated in Sales & Distribution (SD) for both order items and delivery items.
  • Batch classification is mandatory — the batch class (class type 023) must be assigned to the material, and the characteristic LOBM_VFDAT (Shelf Life Expiration Date) must be included and populated on each batch. Source
  • Batches must have the Shelf Life Expiration Date (SLED) maintained in the batch master records so EWM can evaluate and sort them.

Setup Steps

Step 1 — Activate Automatic Batch Determination for Delivery Item Categories

In the S/4HANA Cloud key user configuration:

  1. Go to the configuration activity "Activate Automatic Batch Determination for Delivery Item Categories."
  2. Activate the automatic batch determination flag for the relevant delivery item category used in your outbound delivery. Source

Step 2 — Switch Batch Determination to EWM (Critical Setting)

This step redirects batch assignment from S/4HANA to EWM:

  1. Go to SPRO: Logistics Execution > Extended Warehouse Management Integration > Basic Setup of EWM Connectivity > Maintain Extended WM-Specific Parameters.
  2. For your warehouse number, activate the switch: "Batch Determination in EWM via Batch Attribute Replication."

This ensures S/4HANA sends only the batch selection criteria (not a fixed batch) to EWM with the outbound delivery. Source

Step 3 — Maintain Batch Classification with SLED Characteristic

  1. Open the app "Manage Classes" and confirm (or create) a batch class of type 023 containing the standard characteristic LOBM_VFDAT (Shelf Life Expiration Date).
  2. Assign this batch class to the batch-managed material via "Change Material" (MM02), Classification view.
  3. Ensure all relevant batches have the SLED value populated in the batch master record. Without this, FEFO sorting is silently bypassed.

Step 4 — Create a Sort Rule for FEFO

  1. Open the app "Create Sort Sequence" (or use the configuration activity for sort rules in Batch Management).
  2. Create a sort rule using characteristic LOBM_VFDAT in ascending order (earliest expiry date first = FEFO).

Step 5 — Configure the Batch Search Strategy for Outbound Delivery

  1. Open the app "Manage Search Strategies - Batch."
  2. Select or create a strategy type for Sales/Delivery (e.g., SD01).
  3. Create a batch search strategy for the relevant material/plant combination.
  4. Assign the selection class (from Step 3) and the FEFO sort rule (from Step 4) to the strategy.
  5. Ensure the search strategy is assigned to the correct search procedure, which is in turn assigned to the delivery business transaction. Source

Step 6 — Define How Quantity Is Proposed

  1. Go to the configuration activity "Defining How Quantities are Proposed in Batch Determination."
  2. Set the quantity proposal so the system fills the required delivery quantity automatically across batches (batch split), starting from the earliest-expiring batch. Source

How It Runs End-to-End in "Manage Outbound Delivery Orders"

Once configured:

  1. S/4HANA creates the outbound delivery order and passes batch selection criteria (including SLED characteristics) to EWM.
  2. EWM evaluates available quants, applies the FEFO sort rule (ascending LOBM_VFDAT), and assigns the batch with the earliest expiry date first.
  3. If the earliest batch does not have sufficient quantity, EWM performs a batch split and continues to the next-expiring batch automatically.
  4. The assigned batch(es) and quantities are written back into the S/4HANA outbound delivery document — no manual entry needed. Source

RFQ Approval / Rejection Email Notification to Internal Users

What is happening

The "Maintain Email Templates" app only shows templates for outbound communication to suppliers/bidders by default. There is no dedicated pre-delivered RFQ approval/rejection result template visible out of the box for internal users. This matches a known community case describing exactly the same symptom. Source: SAP Community

SAP's design is that the approval-result notification to internal users (requestor / workflow initiator) is handled via the generic flexible workflow completion template mechanism, not a dedicated RFQ-specific pre-delivered template. You must create the custom templates manually by copying the generic pre-delivered template.

Prerequisites

  • Role: Administrator (SAP_BR_ADMINISTRATOR) to access Maintain Email Templates
  • Role: Configuration expert to access Manage Workflows for RFQs
  • The RFQ flexible workflow (scenario WS00800302) must already be active
  • Recipient user(s) must have a valid email address maintained in the system (Manage Workforce app)

Setup Steps

The RFQ workflow scenario ID is 00800302 (confirmed: SAP Help - Workflow Scenarios and Tasks).

  1. Open the "Maintain Email Templates" app (F1306A).

  2. Go to the "Predelivered" tab and search for the template SWF_WORKFLOW_COMPLETE_NOTIFY.

  3. Select it and choose "Copy".

  4. Save the copy with the following exact names -- one copy per result:

    • For approval: YY1_00800302_COMPLETE_POSITIVE
    • For rejection: YY1_00800302_COMPLETE_NEGATIVE

    Note: Template IDs are limited to 30 characters. Both names above are within that limit.

  5. Adapt the template content (subject, body text) to your needs and save.

  6. Open the "Manage Workflows for RFQs" app.

  7. Locate your active workflow.

  8. Under the Notifications section, select the corresponding custom email template for each workflow result (Approved / Rejected).

  9. Save the workflow configuration.

Once active, the workflow initiator / requestor will receive an email when the RFQ is approved or rejected.

Important notes

  • The templates YY1_00800302_COMPLETE_POSITIVE / YY1_00800302_COMPLETE_NEGATIVE are checked for by name in the flexible workflow code -- the naming convention is hardcoded, so the exact pattern must be followed. Source: SAP Community blog
  • Recipients are predefined by SAP's workflow logic (the workflow initiator / requestor). You cannot freely add arbitrary recipients to this template type.
  • Approvers receiving notifications for pending work items use a different template: SWF_CRT_NOTIFY_RECIPIENTS -- the pattern for that would be YY1_00800302_CRT_ALL.
  • The approval configuration (AV) you mention -- which triggers at the stage of publishing the RFQ to vendors -- is correct by design. The email notification for the completion result (approved/rejected) is a separate configuration layered on top via the templates above.

BAdI and Extensibility Options for Supplier Invoice Item Custom Fields via A2A API

Here is a consolidated picture of what SAP supports, what is not available, and the most viable workarounds.

Why Your Explored BAdIs Did Not Work

BAdI Reason it does not apply

LOG_EDI_MM_INVOICE_CE_MAPBound exclusively to the B2B service InvoiceRequest_In, not the A2A service SupplierInvoiceS4Request_In.
MRM_MRIS_DATA_MODIFY_CENot triggered during invoice posting or parking via Manage Supplier Invoices or the A2A API.
MRM_MRDC_DATA_MODIFY_CEIntended for automatic planned delivery cost settlement (ERS variant), not standard invoice posting.
MRM_ERS_DATA_MODIFY_CEEvaluated Receipt Settlement specific; not triggered in standard invoice posting.

This is confirmed in SAP Help -- BAdIs for Invoice Processing and in the SAP Community thread directly matching your scenario: Guidance Required on BAdI for Updating Supplier Invoice Item-Level Custom Fields via A2A API.

What SAP Actually Supports for A2A + Item Custom Fields

1. Extend the A2A Service Itself via Custom Fields and Logic (Recommended Starting Point)

The SupplierInvoiceS4Request_In service supports extensibility at both header and item level via the Custom Fields app. The relevant business contexts for item-level custom fields are:

  • MM_SI_ITEM -- Supplier Invoice Item with Purchasing Document Ref. / Consignment
  • FINS_CODING_BLOCK -- Supplier Invoice Item, G/L Account Assignment

Once you create and publish a custom field under the correct business context, you can enable it for the SOAP API so that the field is exposed in the inbound message. Your external system can then send the value directly in the SupplierInvoiceS4Request_In payload.

Source: Service Structure -- SupplierInvoiceS4Request_In Extensibility

This means: if your third-party system has access to the PO data and can include the derived values in the outbound SOAP message, the cleanest solution is to populate the custom fields directly in the API payload rather than deriving them server-side via a BAdI.

2. MRM_CHECK_INVOICE_CLOUD -- Validation Only, Not Field Population

This BAdI is triggered during invoice creation (including via A2A) and covers both header and item data. However, it is strictly for custom validation and error messaging -- it cannot modify or populate custom field values. Do not use it as a derivation hook.

Source: BAdIs for Invoice Processing

3. Standard Propagation from PO Item to Invoice Item 

SAP explicitly states that there is no standard propagation of custom fields from purchase order item to supplier invoice item in Public Cloud. Only specific scenarios (for example, PO to delivery) are supported.

Source: SAP KBA 3759817 -- Custom Field On Purchase Order Item Not Propagated

Recommended Approach for Your Scenario

Given that your third-party system uses the A2A service and needs to read PO details to derive values for item-level custom fields, the most feasible approach within the Public Cloud clean-core extensibility model is:

  1. Create the item-level custom fields in the Custom Fields app using business context MM_SI_ITEM.
  2. Enable these fields for the SupplierInvoiceS4Request_In SOAP API in the "APIs" section of the custom field configuration, then publish.
  3. In your third-party system or integration middleware (such as SAP Integration Suite / BTP), read the reference PO details via the Purchase Order OData API (API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV), derive the values, and include them in the SupplierInvoiceS4Request_In payload at item level before posting.

This keeps the derivation logic in the integration layer -- which is where it belongs in A2A scenarios -- rather than relying on a server-side BAdI that does not exist for this service.

If Server-Side Derivation Is Required

There is currently no publicly documented BAdI in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition that fires during A2A inbound supplier invoice processing and allows modification of custom item field values. The B2B equivalent (LOG_EDI_MM_INVOICE_CE_MAP) is not available for the A2A path.

Your options in this case are:

  • Raise an SAP Influence request or open a customer incident to request an equivalent BAdI for SupplierInvoiceS4Request_In (this is the only path to getting a net-new enhancement point in Public Cloud).
  • Validate whether a side-by-side extension using BTP could read the posted invoice via OData, look up the PO, and update the custom field via a subsequent API call -- though this would require the custom field to be writable post-creation, which needs verification for your specific business context.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Based on SAP Note 3835340 and the available SAP documentation, here is the root cause and resolution for your issue.

Root Cause

The KSeF reference number is stored in field FPAYP-REF05(35) during payment processing. However, SAP's standard payment trees (DMEE/CGI formats) do not map this field to any output node by default. This means the KSeF number is not automatically written into the payment medium XML file.

The reason you see the KSeF number in XML for payment method J but not for A and T is most likely that payment method J has already been configured with either:

  • a custom Note to Payee that includes &FPAYP-REF05(35)&, or
  • a custom payment format mapping that maps FPAYP-REF05(35) to the relevant XML node,

while payment methods A and T have not received that same configuration.

Resolution Steps

SAP Note 3835340 describes two approaches to bring the KSeF number into the payment medium XML:

Option 1: Via Note to Payee (recommended approach)

  1. Go to SSCUI 101972 "Set Up Payment Methods for Each Country/Region for Payment Transactions" for Poland.
  2. For payment methods A and T, check which Note to Payee is currently assigned.
  3. Create a copy of the SAP-delivered Note to Payee SAP_CGI_PL.
  4. In the first line of the copied Note to Payee, add the reference &FPAYP-REF05(35)&.
  5. Assign this new Note to Payee to payment methods A and T.

This causes the KSeF reference number to appear in the remittance information of the payment XML (typically the <Ustrd> node in ISO 20022 files).

Option 2: Direct XML node mapping

If you need the KSeF number in a specific XML node other than the Note to Payee / <Ustrd>:

  1. Open the "Map Format Data for Payments" app (SSCUI 100558).
  2. Locate the payment format used by payment methods A and T (for Poland, typically PL_CGI_XML_CT for ISO 20022 credit transfers).
  3. Add a mapping for FPAYP-REF05(35) to the target XML node in the format tree.

Verification

Compare the Note to Payee and format mapping configuration of payment method J with that of A and T. The gap in configuration between J and the other two is the direct cause of the difference in XML output.

  • SAP Note 3835340 - KSeF Reference Number in payment medium files
  • Grouping Payment Items by KSeF Reference Number in Automatic Payments
  • Mapping Fields to the XML File

entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

 

The issue is a fundamental architectural conflict between how the transaction S_P00_07000221 (EC Sales List in DME Format) works and what SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition allows.

Here is what is happening and why:

What the transaction does

S_P00_07000221 runs program RFASLD20, which generates the EC Sales List as a DME (Data Medium Exchange) file. Technically, the program uses the ABAP OPEN DATASET / WRITE DATASET statements to write the output file directly to the SAP application server file system. When it also needs to read an input or test file from the application server (in your case a file named "Test"), it hits an authorization check against the object S_DATASET.

Why you cannot fix it through roles

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, S_DATASET is a low-level ABAP authorization object for direct application-server file access. Customers cannot assign or maintain this object manually. The Public Cloud authorization model works exclusively through business roles, business catalogs, and IAM apps -- there is no way for a customer to grant S_DATASET permissions directly to a user.

The error message itself even points to the on-premise path ("contact your system administrator" to assign S_DATASET), which is not applicable in Public Cloud.

The likely root cause of the "Test" filename

The word "Test" in the error is almost certainly a filename or path value that was entered in the DMEE format tree output configuration or in the selection screen of the report. The program is trying to read or validate a file with that name from the application server before generating output -- and the authorization check for that read fails.

What to check and do

  1. Check the selection screen carefully. Look at the output control section. If there is a field for a file path or filename, the value "Test" has likely been entered there as a placeholder. The transaction expects this to be a valid, authorized path on the application server -- which is not accessible to end users in Public Cloud.

  2. Use the supported cloud process instead. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition offers a different, cloud-native path for EC Sales List reporting. According to SAP documentation, you can use the standard Fiori-based statutory reporting flow, which generates a CSV or XML file and makes it available on an Attachments tab -- without requiring direct application-server file access. The relevant business role template is SAP_BR_GL_ACCOUNTANT_DE (for Germany). Source

  3. Check whether the DME format tree approach is actually required. If your country variant requires DME output specifically, raise an incident with SAP Support. Some DME-based export scenarios for Public Cloud may require a specific configuration or SAP note, and SAP Support can confirm whether the transaction is fully supported in Public Cloud or whether a different reporting path is intended.

  4. Do not attempt to resolve this through S_DATASET. Even if it were technically possible to assign it, it would not resolve the underlying problem that the application server file system is not customer-accessible in Public Cloud the way it is on-premise.

In short: the transaction itself is trying to do something (write/read application-server files) that Public Cloud restricts by design. The path forward is either the cloud-native Fiori statutory reporting app or an SAP Support incident to clarify the supported export mechanism for your country variant.

entry.title: Re: Version Control in SAP Group reporting Public Cloud I...
entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Here is the guidance across your three points, grounded in SAP Help Portal documentation.

Preliminary confirmation: Version setting

Your described assignment matches the SAP-delivered standard content for the 1SG Group Reporting best practice process. The Group Reporting Financial Consolidation business process document (1SG, release 2608) confirms exactly this split:

  • Y10: Data Entry, Consolidation Group Attribute, Structure, Exchange Rates, Reclassification and Eliminations, Reporting Rules, FS Group Items
  • S10: Consolidation Unit Attribute, FS Item Attributes

Source: 1SG Business Process Document, SAP Help Portal

Question 1: Blank local and group currency sources -- what Release Universal Journal transfers and how translation works

When both fields are left blank, the following applies:

Local currency source blank: The system reads amounts in functional currency (FCSL) from ACDOCA as the local currency values for the consolidation unit. No alternative currency type is picked up. This is explicitly documented: "If Local Currency Source is left empty, the system reads amounts in functional currency (FCSL) from ACDOCA as LC values for the consolidation unit."

Source: Important Considerations, SAP Help Portal

Group currency source blank: No group currency amount is copied directly from ACDOCA. Instead, the system transfers only the local currency amounts at posting level blank (reported data). Group currency values are then calculated by running the separate Currency Translation (CT) task in Group Reporting, applying the exchange rate methods and rates configured in the version.

SAP explicitly recommends leaving Group Currency Source blank when the requirement is to translate company code values into different group currencies per consolidation version. If you instead set it to K, the system copies group currency directly from ACDOCA without translation, which means it would only work where the source currency in accounting already matches the target group currency.

Source: SAP Note 3706725, "Assign consistent group currency types to CC if relevant for group reporting"

Summary of the blank/blank flow:

  1. Release Universal Journal reads functional currency amounts from ACDOCA as local currency and transfers them to ACDOCU at posting level blank.
  2. No group currency value is carried over from accounting.
  3. After release, you run Currency Translation in Group Reporting to derive group currency amounts from the transferred local currency amounts.

Question 2: Y10 as SAP-delivered content, sharing special versions with L10, and when to create a separate one

Is Y10 SAP-delivered standard content?

Yes. SAP explicitly delivers Y10 as a template consolidation version for actuals in the standard system. The documentation states: "The system offers several template consolidation versions, such as actuals (Y10 and Y20), budget (YB*), year-end forecast (YF*), actuals using budget exchange rates (Y11), and actuals using simulated exchange rates (Y12)."

Source: Consolidation Versions, SAP Help Portal

The Set Global Parameters activity confirms this and shows Y10 (and Y20, YB*, YF*, Y11, Y12) as preset template versions.

Source: Set Global Parameters, SAP Help Portal

When you create L10 using "Create Version from Reference Version," Y10 and S10 will be offered because they are the only special versions currently present in the system. You can assign L10 to the same Y10 and S10 special versions as your actuals version.

Can L10 share the same special versions as your actuals version?

Technically, yes -- the architecture of special versions is designed precisely to enable this. "The assignment of special versions enables reuse of the maintained settings across consolidation versions."

Source: Group Reporting (FIN-CS) Guide, SAP Help Portal

However, sharing has concrete implications you need to evaluate:

Implications of sharing Y10 across L10 and your actuals version:

Area Implication of sharing Y10

Data EntryL10 and actuals use the same data entry forms and layout. Changes to data entry configuration affect both versions simultaneously.
Consolidation Group Attributes / StructureGroup structure, consolidation units, and group attributes are shared. Any structural change (e.g., adding or removing a unit, changing the group hierarchy) in Y10 applies to both versions.
Exchange RatesBoth versions use the same exchange rate types mapped to exchange rate indicators. If L10 needs different rates (e.g., budget rates vs. actual rates), sharing Y10 is not appropriate.
Reclassification and EliminationsThe same elimination and reclassification methods apply. Any rule change or new method in Y10 affects both.
Reporting Rules and FS Group ItemsSame FS item structure and reporting rules.
Consolidation Unit Attributes (S10)Local currency settings and FS item attributes are shared. Changing a consolidation unit attribute in S10 affects all versions pointing to it.

SAP also notes that some version settings can only be defined at creation time and cannot be changed afterwards. This makes it especially important to decide the special version assignment correctly before creating L10.

Source: Set Global Parameters, SAP Help Portal

When should you create a separate special version for L10?

Create a separate special version in the following situations:

  • Exchange rates differ: This is the most common reason. SAP explicitly uses actuals vs. budget as the example: "Consolidation versions for actuals data and planning data can share all special version settings except that for Exchange Rates. In this case, you can assign different Exchange Rates special versions to each consolidation version." If L10 needs different rate types (e.g., budget or forecast rates instead of actual closing/average rates), you must create a dedicated Exchange Rates special version for L10.

Source: Group Reporting (FIN-CS) Guide, 2022

  • Different elimination or reclassification logic: If L10 requires different intercompany elimination methods or different document type assignments from your actuals version, create a separate Reclassification and Eliminations special version.

  • Different organizational scope: If L10 is intended to consolidate a different set of entities, different group attributes, or a different hierarchy structure, a separate special version for Structure/Consolidation Group Attributes is needed.

  • Regulatory or accounting standard isolation: If L10 must produce consolidated financials under a different standard (e.g., local GAAP vs. IFRS), isolation via separate special versions ensures that rule changes for one standard do not affect the other.

  • Auditability and change control: Even where sharing is technically possible, separate special versions for exchange rates and elimination rules give you independent version control over each consolidation run. This is often preferred in regulated environments.

In practice for your L10 scenario: If L10 is a new version used for a different purpose (e.g., a different legal/management consolidation, a different currency scope, or an alternative set of exchange rates), the minimum recommendation is to create a dedicated Exchange Rates special version for L10, while potentially sharing Y10 for structure, data entry, and FS group items if those are identical. All other special versions can be evaluated based on whether L10 requires independent configuration or can safely inherit from Y10.

Sources used:

  • Consolidation Versions, SAP Help Portal
  • Set Global Parameters, SAP Help Portal
  • Important Considerations for Release Universal Journal, SAP Help Portal
  • SAP Note 3706725 -- Group Currency Source behavior
  • 1SG Business Process Document (2608), SAP Help Portal
  • Group Reporting (FIN-CS) Guide 2022, SAP Help Portal

entry.content:

What's new in 2611: five spotlights across the portfolio

Not all 197+ innovations in the 2611 Supply Chain Management (SCM) portfolio demand the same attention. Here are five that signal where the most significant capability shifts are happening.

ProductDescription

SAP Asset Performance Management: Joule integration and four Agents

  • This release brings Joule to SAP Asset Performance Management (APM) with both navigational and transactional use cases. It's the product's first full Joule integration, and it ships alongside four named Agents: the Asset Performance Alert Processing Agent, Asset Performance Health Analysis Agent, Asset Performance Risk Assessment Agent, and Reliability Case Management Agent.
  • Each Agent covers a distinct part of the reliability engineering workflow: alerting, health trend analysis, risk quantification, and case lifecycle management. Three capabilities are already delivered in 2611: a redesigned Monitor Alerts app, the ability to assign a processor to an alert, and a user-facing change log for alert details. The Agents and Joule integration are planned for the 2611 release window.

SAP Business Network: GenAI PDF invoice conversion and four Collaboration Agents

  • The most broadly applicable new capability in SAP Business Network's 2611 roadmap is generative AI-driven PDF invoice conversion. Suppliers who send PDF invoices can have those documents converted automatically, reducing manual processing on both sides of the transaction. Four Collaboration Agents span the order-to-payment cycle: the Order Confirmation Collaboration Agent, Advanced Ship Notice Collaboration Agent, Service Entry Collaboration Agent, and Invoice Collaboration Agent.
  • A fifth Agent handles autonomous supplier profile updates through web crawlers, keeping trading partner data current without manual input.

SAP Field Service and Asset Management: 12 AI/Agent capabilities, with Joule already delivered

  • SAP Field Service and Asset Management ships the largest AI footprint in this release: 12 capabilities. Joule availability in the admin portal is already delivered in 2611. Joule is also planned for the extension management app and screen configuration app. The Agents span the full service delivery cycle: the Dispatcher Service Agent, Crew Planning and Management Agent, Resource Reservations Management Agent, Business Rules Management Agent, and Field Service System Administration Management Agent.
  • For operations teams running complex scheduling, the Dispatcher Service Agent and Crew Planning and Management Agent together cover the two manual steps that consume the most planning time. That's a real reduction in dispatcher workload, not a marginal one.

SAP Logistics Management: four warehouse and transport Agents

  • SAP Logistics Management ships four Agents targeting the warehouse and transport layer: the Logistics Issue Resolution Agent, Logistics Configuration Agent, Internal Stock Replenishment Agent, and Outbound Warehouse Task Management Agent. For transport, the Transportation Dispatching Agent adds automated dispatching for Full Truck Load (FTL) outbound shipments.
  • Two capabilities are already delivered: handling of Sales Order Stock type E and Handling Unit Numbering. Physical inventory also receives targeted improvements for empty bin handling, unavailable bins, and processor assignment.

SAP Integrated Business Planning: 25 planning improvements

  • SAP Integrated Business Planning (SAP IBP) ships 25 innovations in 2611. Three connected capabilities address planning filter governance at scale: administrators can now view all planning filters system-wide on a new All (Admin) tab, assign human-readable IDs to filters for cleaner documentation and team handoffs, and search for filters by attribute to narrow a large library to the relevant entries. For anyone who's managed a shared IBP environment with dozens of teams, that filter sprawl is a real pain point, and these three changes land together rather than being spread across releases.
  • Two further items stand out: improved job template performance for configurations using SAP Cloud Integration for Data Services (CI-DS), controlled via two new global configuration parameters; and a fix to the time profile extension restriction, which now lets you extend the end date of the last period even when the Allow Extension Only check is active.
  • One deprecation to plan for: the Status, Project, and Project Description columns in the Import Collection app are deprecated in 2611 and will be removed in IBP 2705. Teams using these columns should begin migration planning now.

 

Product area highlights

SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP)

  • The 2611 SAP IBP release focuses on operational stability and governance rather than new planning logic. The three planning filter improvements ship as a coordinated set, a rare instance where related capabilities in the same app arrive together and make their combined impact more than the sum of the parts. The CI-DS buffer parameters require a one-time configuration step and deliver immediate return for customers running large automated data pipelines. The time profile extension fix resolves a situation that previously forced administrators to choose between calendar flexibility and data integrity protection.
  • IBP 2705 will remove the deprecated Import Collection columns. Treat the 2611 window as the migration prompt if your team uses those columns.
  • Check out more information on the SAP IBP page in the Release Navigator for Supply Chain Management.

SAP Digital Manufacturing

  • SAP Digital Manufacturing ships five focused capabilities in 2611. Edge computing support for mission-critical processes extends offline and low-latency operation at the shop floor level. OPC UA server capability is planned, meaningful for manufacturers running heterogeneous equipment networks that currently require custom middleware for machine communication. The two printed circuit board (PCB) capabilities (PCB initialization and identification, and PCB data collection) are specialized but signal continued investment in electronics manufacturing scenarios that standard execution systems have historically underserved.
  • Check out more information on the SAP Digital Manufacturing page in the Release Navigator for Supply Chain Management.

SAP Logistics Management

  • The four warehouse Agents are the most significant AI milestone for SAP Logistics Management since the product's general availability in February 2026. The Logistics Issue Resolution Agent and Logistics Configuration Agent operate at the administration and troubleshooting layer. The Internal Stock Replenishment Agent and Outbound Warehouse Task Management Agent cover physical warehouse execution. Mobile app improvements add no-stock action support, task queue item counts, and product and handling unit move operations, reducing screen navigation for warehouse associates. Support for additional European languages and Hindi is already delivered.
  • Check out more information on the SAP Logistics Management page in the Release Navigator for Supply Chain Management.

SAP Asset Performance Management (APM)

  • SAP APM carries the deepest AI investment in the 2611 SCM portfolio: 10 AI and Agent capabilities across four capability clusters. Anomaly detection gains lifecycle management features in this release: guided training configuration, notification-driven training period setup, and failure diagnostics. The Reliability Case Management Agent covers case lifecycle; the Asset Performance Risk Assessment Agent covers risk quantification; a new data product for recommendations surfaces maintenance guidance automatically.
  • For asset-intensive industries running predictive maintenance programs, this release moves anomaly detection from a monitoring tool toward a system with managed training, observable lifecycle stages, and Agent-driven case handling. That's a meaningful architectural shift.
  • Check out more information on the SAP Asset Performance Management page in the Release Navigator for Supply Chain Management.

SAP Field Service and Asset Management

  • The scheduling and dispatching cluster sees the most Agent activity: the Dispatcher Service Agent and Crew Planning and Management Agent address the two most time-consuming manual steps in field service planning, and the Resource Reservations Management Agent handles technician availability tracking alongside them. On the dispatcher experience side, there's activity card redesign, advanced Service Map filters, multi-technician calendar view, semi-automatic planning from the service map, and time zone handling during the planning process. GDPR-compliant location obfuscation for technicians is also planned. Getting Agent automation and interface improvements in the same release is not the default. This one does.
  • Check out more information on the SAP Field Service and Asset Management page in the Release Navigator for Supply Chain Management.

SAP Integrated Product Development (IDP)

  • SAP IPD ships the largest feature set in the 2611 portfolio: 57 items spanning bill of materials management, CAD tool interoperability, document management, change management, and specification management. The AI cluster concentrates in product and data collaboration: the Product Development Collaboration Agent, Product Knowledge Retrieval Agent, and Product Task Validation Agent bring Agent-driven oversight to the product lifecycle collaboration layer. AI-powered document extraction for specification management automates extraction of structured content from unstructured documents, cutting manual entry in formulation and regulatory workflows. The Smart Recommender for manufacturing BOMs assists in deriving manufacturing bills of materials during product handover.
  • Check out more information on the SAP Integrated Product Development page in the Release Navigator for Supply Chain Management.

SAP Business Network

  • Beyond the Collaboration Agents and GenAI PDF invoice conversion, SAP Business Network 2611 includes enterprise structure replication of SAP ERP organizational data for buyers and suppliers, reducing manual configuration when new trading partners join the network. The Network data intelligence benchmark dashboard, enabled by data-visualization agents, gives procurement teams a comparative view of supplier performance across the network.
  • Check out more information on the SAP Business Network page in the Release Navigator for Supply Chain Management.

 

Navigate 2611 with the Release Navigator for Supply Chain Management

The Release Navigator for Supply Chain Management is available through SAP Foundational Support. It covers all seven products in this post, organized by product area, with key dates, feature highlights, scope item links, and enablement resources for the 2611 release.

  • Start with your product area, open the What's New content for 2611, and identify which features your team is planning to activate first. Which feature capability in the 2611 portfolio are you most interested in deploying, and what workflow are you planning to hand off to it? Drop your answer in the comments. If you've already started your 2611 activation planning, the community would benefit from hearing your approach.
  • Join the conversation. Tag your posts with `Supply Chain Management` and `2611` so the right people find them.

What comes after 2611

The next quarterly release for SAP IBP is 2702, expected in February 2027. Planned items for 2702 include initial delivery of the harmonized planning area and initial aggregated constraints capability.

  • For the broader SCM portfolio, SAP Logistics Management, APM, and SAP Field Service and Asset Management follow the same quarterly cadence. The 2702 window in late Q1 2027 will be the next delivery wave for Agents currently listed as planned in 2611.
  • For forward planning beyond 2702, the SAP Road Map Explorer lets you filter by product and quarter to see what's planned, in development, and recently delivered. Worth bookmarking if you haven't already.

entry.title: Re: How Can We Predict CTS Import Errors Before Productio...
entry.content:
Hi,

I think I can explain why the test import passed, and what I would use instead. This comes from the SAP Help and from what I read in my S/4HANA 2023 lab:

  • The test import is not a dry run of the import. The SAP Help page "Testing Imports" lists two checks: if the objects are in an open repair in the target system, and if the objects in the target system are the originals. Neither looks at dependent objects, so a positive result says nothing about your failure.
  • In BW the problem shows up later. In table OBJM, 100 object types, including ADSO, IOBJ and TRFN, have RS_AFTER_IMPORT as their after-import method, so their activation runs after the objects arrive. As I read it, that is where a missing object fails, and the test import doesn't get there.

What I would add to your pre-checks:

  1. Program RSO_TLOGO_CHECK_REQUEST, "BW Consistency Check of a Transport Request", in the development system. It collects the dependent objects of each BW object in the request. Error RSO 657 says that an object needs another one that is not in a request, and there is a warning when that other object is only on requests not yet released. The same class, CL_RSO_TLOGO_BEFORE_EXPORT, also runs at release through CTS_REQUEST_CHECK, so please look at table RSTPCHECKEXC: a row with * in all key fields switches the check off, which could be why you don't see these messages.
  2. Close its gap by hand. That check reads E070 and E071 in the development system, so a dependent object on a released request passes even if that request never reached production. For each dependent request, check the production import history in STMS, or ask your transport team to, since you don't import yourselves.
  3. For a real simulation, the only way I know is to import into a recent copy of production, in the same order you will use there. QAS predicts production only while it has the same imports in the same order.

SAP's learning material also cites Note 2510475 "Simulate Transport". I couldn't read that note, so it is worth a look with your S-user.

I only read the help page, the code and the tables, and my lab is S/4HANA with its embedded BW, not BW/4HANA, so please confirm that the program and the table exist in your system. I didn't run the program on a request or reproduce your failure, and I can't read the tp program itself, so the point about the test import not reaching the after-import step comes from the help page and not from a trace. If you can share the failing step and return code from the import log, I'm happy to look at them with you.

I think the field is there, only under another name. PurgDocItem and PurgOrderItem show the raw name BSGRU, but the VDM views call it PurchasingOrderReason, which may be why a search for BSGRU doesn't find them.

In SAP's public Cloudification Repository (SAP/abap-atc-cr-cv-s4hc, public cloud file objectReleaseInfoLatest.json), these three are listed as released:

  • I_PurchaseOrderItemAPI01
  • I_PurchaseOrderItemTP_2
  • C_PurchaseOrderItemDEX

In my S/4HANA 2023 lab, the sources of all three have both PurchasingOrderReason and IsReturnsItem. So to read the field in a custom CDS view, I would use I_PurchaseOrderItemAPI01 as the data source.

One thing before you build it: if your validation runs in the BAdI BD_MMPUR_FINAL_CHECK_PO, also listed as released, a view may not help. The view reads the database and the check runs before the save, so for a new purchase order it finds nothing, and for a change it finds the old value. The BAdI itself gets the items as they are being edited, including isreturnsitem, but in my 2023 lab its item structure has no reason field. If that is the same in your release, I would look at MM_PUR_S4_PO_FLDCNTRL_SIMPLE, listed as released too. It receives the item, so you can test isreturnsitem, and it returns a status per field, with mandatory as one of the options. That would make the field required, instead of checking it afterwards.

What I didn't test: I don't have a Public Cloud system, so the field names come from the 2023 sources and the release state from SAP's file, so please confirm them in your View Browser. entry.title: Re: RAP unmanaged BO: BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC dump...
entry.content:
Hi,

Very clear question, thank you for laying out the options. I read the code in my S/4HANA 2023 lab, the same release as yours, maybe another FPS, and for this app I would stay with A. Here is why:

  • B can't be made safe. The BAPI calls PERFORM rollback_check, and that form (LV50IF01) only checks the internal flag gf_flag-rollback, set when an error comes back, and then runs ROLLBACK WORK. I didn't find a parameter that switches it off, so pre-checks will always miss a case, like your OKB9 one.
  • SAP's own API behaves the same way. API_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV has a PostGoodsIssue action, which ends in CL_OD_API_HEADER_PROCESS, method PGI. Outside a changeset, that method runs ROLLBACK WORK on error and COMMIT WORK AND WAIT on success, so the API owns its own commit.
  • The main con of A matters little here. Your BO has no persistence and no draft, so PGI is the only write in the request, and the RAP LUW has nothing else to stay consistent with. If you later add other changes to the same request, I would move to C. For the lock, you already get "delivery locked" back from the BAPI, so I would leave it to the BAPI.

One small tip for A: if you don't pass WAIT = 'X' to BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT, reading the delivery right after the action can still show the old status.

About your other questions:

  • sRFC in the interaction phase: I don't know. I looked at a few entries of the ABAP documentation in my lab and found nothing about it in either direction, so I can't promise it stays allowed.
  • Uncontrolled bgPF from save: as I read it, yes. SET_OPERATION_TX_UNCONTROLLED is classified as functional in IF_BGMC_PROCESS_SINGLE_OP, SAVE_FOR_EXECUTION is classified as save in IF_BGMC_PROCESS, and IF_BGMC_OP_SINGLE_TX_UNCONTR is released for contract C1 in my lab and also listed as released in SAP's public cloud file.
  • A released RAP BO with PGI: I didn't find one either. The OData API above is the closest I found, and calling it through a loopback, the way Ali described, should give the same transaction behavior as A.

What I didn't test: I only read the sources. I didn't run any of the options or the API, and I can't speak for newer releases. If you try the bgPF route, I would be curious to know how it behaves.

entry.title: Re: Can AIF error alerts be delivered to SAP Business Wor...
entry.content:
Hi,

I think it can work, through Alert Management and not through an AIF setting, but I only read the code and didn't run it, so please test it with one user first.

What I read in my S/4HANA 2023 lab:

  1. AIF alerts are ordinary Alert Management alerts. The category /AIF/ALERT_CAT_DEF is in table SALRTCAT, and the AIF recipient table I looked at, /AIF/IF_RECIPIENT, only assigns recipients to interfaces. I didn't find an AIF option for SAPoffice.
  2. Delivery is decided per user, in table SALRTDLVRY, field EMAIL, "Send Alert by E-Mail". In class CL_ALERT_MANAGER, method GET_USER_PERSONALIZATION, a user without a row gets one with EMAIL switched on. So this path may already be active for your users.
  3. Method SEND of the same class reads the user's default communication method. It keeps INT or RML, and anything else becomes INT.

So with INT the alert leaves as an external e-mail. For SBWP, the setting I would try is RML as the default communication method of that user in SU01, with the RML address maintained, and the SAP connection node set up in SCOT. As far as I know, RML is the type that delivers to a SAP inbox, but this is the part I couldn't confirm in the code, so it is the first thing to check.

To test it, I would raise one AIF error for a test user and look in SOST. If the document is there and waiting, the gap is in SAPconnect. If it isn't, I would check that user's personalization in the Alert Inbox.

One thing to watch: the default communication method is not only for alerts, so changing it can also change how other documents reach those users.

If you try it, please share what you see, because I would like to know if it lands in the inbox.
